final answer
## PCI PM callback chain reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

In `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`, the PM table is:

```c
const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops = {
	.suspend          = i915_pm_suspend,
	.suspend_late     = i915_pm_suspend_late,
	.suspend_noirq    = i915_pm_suspend_noirq,
	...
	.freeze           = i915_pm_freeze,
	...
	.poweroff         = i915_pm_suspend,
	.poweroff_late    = i915_pm_poweroff_late,
	.poweroff_noirq   = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq,
	...
	.runtime_suspend  = intel_runtime_suspend,
};
```

Therefore, the only PCI/system-PM callback entries that reach `i915_pm_suspend` are:

### 1. System suspend

```text
PM core
  └─ dev_pm_ops.suspend
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev) → i915
            ├─ skip if DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF
            └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                 └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(dev_priv->display)
```

Relevant code:

- `i915_pm_ops.suspend = i915_pm_suspend` — `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1719`
- `i915_pm_suspend()` — lines `1392–1405`
- `i915_pm_suspend()` calls `i915_drm_suspend()` at line `1404`

### 2. Hibernation image poweroff

```text
PM core
  └─ dev_pm_ops.poweroff
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev) → i915
            ├─ skip if DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF
            └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                 └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(dev_priv->display)
```

This is the same function, registered a second time:

- `i915_pm_ops.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend` — line `1745`

Thus, both `.suspend` and `.poweroff` share the identical call chain after dispatch.

## Other PCI PM callbacks

These do **not** reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
.suspend_late      → i915_pm_suspend_late → i915_drm_suspend_late
.suspend_noirq     → i915_pm_suspend_noirq → i915_drm_suspend_noirq
.poweroff_late     → i915_pm_poweroff_late → i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)
.poweroff_noirq    → i915_pm_poweroff_noirq → i915_drm_suspend_noirq(..., true)
.freeze            → i915_pm_freeze → i915_drm_suspend directly
.runtime_suspend   → intel_runtime_suspend
```

`i915_pm_freeze()` also invokes the common suspend routine, but it calls `i915_drm_suspend()` directly rather than going through `i915_pm_suspend`.

## Which callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`?

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in this tree.

The runtime PM callback is named:

```text
intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
```

and is registered as:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend;
```

It does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()` or `i915_drm_suspend()`. It follows a separate runtime-suspend path:

```text
intel_runtime_suspend
  ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
  ├─ intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(...)
  ├─ intel_gt_runtime_suspend(...)
  ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
  ├─ intel_uncore_suspend(...)
  ├─ intel_display_power_suspend(display)
  └─ vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv)
```

Consequently:

- `i915_pm_suspend`: does not call runtime suspend
- `.poweroff` → `i915_pm_suspend`: does not call runtime suspend
- `intel_runtime_suspend`: is not a caller of `i915_pm_suspend`
- No callback calls a function named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The current tree does not contain a function named `intel_display_suspend`; the corresponding function is `intel_display_driver_suspend()` in `display/intel_display_driver.c`.

The data flow is:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  │
  ├─ struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  │
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
       │
       ├─ struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
       │
       ├─ struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display
       │
       └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
            │
            ├─ HAS_DISPLAY(display)
            ├─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
            ├─ display->restore.modeset_state = state
            ├─ flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)
            └─ intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
```

Specifically, `i915_drm_suspend()` does not pass `dev_priv` directly to the display function. It derives the display object:

```c
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
...
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
```

Then `intel_display_driver_suspend()` obtains the DRM device indirectly from the display object:

```c
state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
```

So the effective object flow is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  → struct drm_i915_private *i915/dev_priv
  → struct drm_device (&dev_priv->drm)
  → struct intel_display *display (dev_priv->display)
  → struct drm_device (display->drm)
  → drm_atomic_helper_suspend()
```

## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The i915 driver registers `i915_pm_suspend` as its normal system-suspend callback:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1718–1724`
  - `.suspend = i915_pm_suspend`

The PCI PM framework reaches it through these callback paths:

```text
pci_pm_suspend()
  → pm_generic_suspend()
    → driver->pm->suspend()
      → i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                 [i915_driver.c:1392]
        → kdev_to_i915(kdev)
          → i915 = struct drm_i915_private *
        → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)        [i915_driver.c:1404]
```

For poweroff/hibernation:

```text
pci_pm_poweroff()
  → pm_generic_poweroff()
    → driver->pm->poweroff()
      → i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                 [shared suspend callback path]
        → kdev_to_i915(kdev)
        → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The direct i915 callback relationship indexed by codegraph is:

```text
pci_pm_suspend   → i915_pm_suspend
pci_pm_poweroff  → i915_pm_suspend
```

The i915 PM callback itself first handles the absent-device and switcheroo-off cases:

```c
struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

if (!i915)
        return -ENODEV;

if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
        return 0;

return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
```

### Other in-tree i915 callers of `i915_drm_suspend`

These are not PCI PM callback paths, but they also reach the same suspend implementation:

```text
i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(i915, state)
  → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

i915_pm_freeze(kdev)
  → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

`i915_pm_suspend` itself is the normal callback that also invokes `i915_drm_suspend`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the PCI PM callback paths that reach `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

They are separate PM domains:

```text
System suspend:
pci_pm_suspend / pci_pm_poweroff
  → i915_pm_suspend
    → i915_drm_suspend

Runtime suspend:
runtime PM core
  → i915_pm_runtime_suspend
```

Thus, among the callers in the PCI/system-suspend chain:

| Caller | Reaches `i915_pm_suspend` | Also calls `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `pci_pm_suspend` | Yes | No |
| `pci_pm_poweroff` | Yes | No |

## `dev_priv` data flow to the display suspend routine

The indexed source names the display routine `intel_display_driver_suspend`; there is no indexed `intel_display_suspend` symbol in this tree. The data flow is:

```text
pci_pm_suspend()
  → i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
      i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            └─ dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
               → struct drm_i915_private *i915
      i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

  → i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
      dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
                └─ recover containing drm_i915_private
                   → same i915 object
      display = dev_priv->display
      intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Relevant source locations:

- `i915_pm_suspend`: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1392–1405`
- `i915_drm_suspend`: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1103–1148`
- `dev_priv` initialization:
  - `struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);`
- Display object extraction:
  - `struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;`
- Display suspend call:
  - `intel_display_driver_suspend(display);` at line `1120`

In other words, `dev_priv` is not copied or reconstructed between the two functions: `kdev_to_i915()` obtains the i915 private structure from the device driver data, `&i915->drm` is passed upward as the DRM device, and `to_i915()` recovers the same containing `struct drm_i915_private`; its `display` member is then passed to the display suspend routine.

int i915_driver_resume_switcheroo(struct drm_i915_private *i915)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(i915->drm.dev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	ret = pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D0);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	pci_restore_state(pdev);

	ret = i915_drm_resume_early(&i915->drm);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return i915_drm_resume(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_prepare(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_prepare(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	/*
	 * We have a suspend ordering issue with the snd-hda driver also
	 * requiring our device to be power up. Due to the lack of a
	 * parent/child relationship we currently solve this with an late
	 * suspend hook.
	 *
	 * FIXME: This should be solved with a special hdmi sink device or
	 * similar so that power domains can be employed.
	 */
	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
}

static bool suspend_to_idle(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)
{
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_ACPI_SLEEP)
	if (acpi_target_system_state() < ACPI_STATE_S3)
		return true;
#endif
	return false;
}

static void i915_drm_complete(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = to_i915(dev);

	intel_pxp_resume_complete(i915->pxp);
}

static int i915_drm_prepare(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = to_i915(dev);

	intel_pxp_suspend_prepare(i915->pxp);

	/*
	 * NB intel_display_driver_suspend() may issue new requests after we've
	 * ostensibly marked the GPU as ready-to-sleep here. We need to
	 * split out that work and pull it forward so that after point,
	 * the GPU is not woken again.
	 */
	return i915_gem_backup_suspend(i915);
}

static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	pci_power_t opregion_target_state;

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	/* We do a lot of poking in a lot of registers, make sure they work
	 * properly. */
	intel_power_domains_disable(display);
	drm_client_dev_suspend(dev);
	if (intel_display_device_present(display)) {
		drm_kms_helper_poll_disable(dev);
		intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display);
	}

	intel_display_driver_suspend(display);

	intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv);
	intel_hpd_cancel_work(display);

	if (intel_display_device_present(display))
		intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display);

	intel_encoder_suspend_all(display);

	/* Must be called before GGTT is suspended. */
	intel_dpt_suspend(display);
	i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt);

	i9xx_display_sr_save(display);

	opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) ? PCI_D1 : PCI_D3cold;
	intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state);

	dev_priv->suspend_count++;

	intel_dmc_suspend(display);

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv);

	return 0;
}

static int i915_drm_suspend_late(struct drm_device *dev, bool hibernation)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	struct intel_runtime_pm *rpm = &dev_priv->runtime_pm;
	struct intel_gt *gt;
	int ret, i;
	bool s2idle = !hibernation && suspend_to_idle(dev_priv);

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	intel_pxp_suspend(dev_priv->pxp);

	i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore);

	intel_display_power_suspend_late(display, s2idle);

	ret = vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv);
	if (ret) {
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm, "Suspend complete failed: %d\n", ret);
		intel_display_power_resume_early(display);
	}

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	if (!dev_priv->uncore.user_forcewake_count)
		intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm);

	return ret;
}

static int i915_drm_suspend_noirq(struct drm_device *dev, bool hibernation)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(dev_priv->drm.dev);

	/*
	 * During hibernation on some platforms the BIOS may try to access
	 * the device even though it's already in D3 and hang the machine. So
	 * leave the device in D0 on those platforms and hope the BIOS will
	 * power down the device properly. The issue was seen on multiple old
	 * GENs with different BIOS vendors, so having an explicit blacklist
	 * is impractical; apply the workaround on everything pre GEN6. The
	 * platforms where the issue was seen:
	 * Lenovo Thinkpad X301, X61s, X60, T60, X41
	 * Fujitsu FSC S7110
	 * Acer Aspire 1830T
	 *
	 * pci_save_state() prevents drivers/pci from
	 * automagically putting the device into D3.
	 */
	if (hibernation && GRAPHICS_VER(dev_priv) < 6)
		pci_save_state(pdev);

	return 0;
}

int i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(struct drm_i915_private *i915,
				   pm_message_t state)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(i915->drm.dev);
	int error;

	if (drm_WARN_ON_ONCE(&i915->drm, state.event != PM_EVENT_SUSPEND &&
			     state.event != PM_EVENT_FREEZE))
		return -EINVAL;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	error = i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
	if (error)
		return error;

	error = i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
	if (error)
		return error;

	pci_save_state(pdev);
	pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D3hot);

	return 0;
}

{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);

{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

static void i915_pm_complete(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return;

	i915_drm_complete(&i915->drm);
}

/* freeze: before creating the hibernation_image */
static int i915_pm_freeze(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

static int i915_pm_freeze_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze_late(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

/* thaw: called after creating the hibernation image, but before turning off. */
static int i915_pm_thaw_early(struct device *kdev)
{
	return i915_pm_resume_early(kdev);
}

static int i915_pm_thaw(struct device *kdev)
{
	return i915_pm_resume(kdev);
}

/* restore: called after loading the hibernation image. */
static int i915_pm_restore_early(struct device *kdev)
{
	return i915_pm_resume_early(kdev);
}

static int i915_pm_restore(struct device *kdev)
{
	return i915_pm_resume(kdev);
}

static int intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{

		return -ENODEV;

	i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt);

{

}

#include <linux/vga_switcheroo.h>

#include "i915_drv.h"
#include "i915_switcheroo.h"

static void i915_switcheroo_set_state(struct pci_dev *pdev,
				      enum vga_switcheroo_state state)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = pdev_to_i915(pdev);
	struct intel_display *display = i915 ? i915->display : NULL;
	pm_message_t pmm = { .event = PM_EVENT_SUSPEND };

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "DRM not initialized, aborting switch.\n");
		return;
	}
	if (!intel_display_device_present(display)) {
		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Device state not initialized, aborting switch.\n");
		return;
	}

	if (state == VGA_SWITCHEROO_ON) {
		drm_info(&i915->drm, "switched on\n");
		i915->drm.switch_power_state = DRM_SWITCH_POWER_CHANGING;
		/* i915 resume handler doesn't set to D0 */
		pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D0);
		i915_driver_resume_switcheroo(i915);
		i915->drm.switch_power_state = DRM_SWITCH_POWER_ON;
	} else {
		drm_info(&i915->drm, "switched off\n");
		i915->drm.switch_power_state = DRM_SWITCH_POWER_CHANGING;
		i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(i915, pmm);
		i915->drm.switch_power_state = DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF;
	}
}

static bool i915_switcheroo_can_switch(struct pci_dev *pdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = pdev_to_i915(pdev);
	struct intel_display *display = i915 ? i915->display : NULL;

	/*
	 * FIXME: open_count is protected by drm_global_mutex but that would lead to
	 * locking inversion with the driver load path. And the access here is
	 * completely racy anyway. So don't bother with locking for now.
	 */
	return i915 && intel_display_device_present(display) &&
		atomic_read(&i915->drm.open_count) == 0;
}

static const struct vga_switcheroo_client_ops i915_switcheroo_ops = {
	.set_gpu_state = i915_switcheroo_set_state,
	.reprobe = NULL,
	.can_switch = i915_switcheroo_can_switch,
};

final answer
In this tree, the PCI PM callbacks are supplied through `i915_pm_ops` in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1713`
- Registered by `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:1025-1032`

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` or `intel_display_suspend` symbol in this source tree. The corresponding functions are `intel_runtime_suspend` and `intel_display_driver_suspend`.

## PM callback call chains

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM .suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            -> to_i915(dev)             // dev_priv
            -> dev_priv->display         // display
            -> intel_power_domains_disable(display)
            -> drm_client_dev_suspend(dev)
            -> intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
            -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
            -> intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
            -> intel_hpd_cancel_work(display)
            -> intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
            -> intel_encoder_suspend_all(display)
            -> intel_dpt_suspend(display)
            -> i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)
            -> i9xx_display_sr_save(display)
            -> intel_opregion_suspend(display, ...)
            -> intel_dmc_suspend(display)
            -> i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)
```

Locations:

- `i915_pm_suspend`: `i915_driver.c:1392`
- `i915_drm_suspend`: `i915_driver.c:1103`
- `intel_display_driver_suspend`: `display/intel_display_driver.c:684`

### System suspend-late

```text
PCI PM .suspend_late
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
            -> intel_pxp_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
            -> i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv)
            -> intel_uncore_suspend(...)
            -> intel_display_power_suspend_late(display, ...)
            -> vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv)
            -> intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm)
```

This does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend` or `i915_drm_suspend`.

### System suspend-noirq

```text
PCI PM .suspend_noirq
  -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)
            -> possibly pci_save_state(pdev)
```

This does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend` or `i915_drm_suspend`.

### Hibernation freeze

```text
PCI PM .freeze
  -> i915_pm_freeze(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            -> [same chain shown under system suspend]
       -> i915_gem_freeze(i915)
```

This reaches the same suspend implementation as `i915_pm_suspend`, but it calls `i915_drm_suspend` directly rather than calling `i915_pm_suspend`.

### Hibernation freeze-late

```text
PCI PM .freeze_late
  -> i915_pm_freeze_late(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
       -> i915_gem_freeze_late(i915)
```

No call to `i915_pm_suspend`.

### Hibernation poweroff

```text
PCI PM .poweroff
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            -> [same chain shown under system suspend]
```

This is the second PM callback that directly uses `i915_pm_suspend`.

### Hibernation poweroff-late

```text
PCI PM .poweroff_late
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
```

No call to `i915_pm_suspend`.

### Hibernation poweroff-noirq

```text
PCI PM .poweroff_noirq
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
```

No call to `i915_pm_suspend`.

### Runtime suspend

```text
PCI PM .runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)             // dev_priv
       -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
       -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
       -> intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
       -> display/runtime power handling
       -> PCI power-state handling
```

`intel_runtime_suspend` does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend` or `i915_drm_suspend`.

### Resume/thaw/restore callbacks

```text
.resume_early
  -> i915_pm_resume_early
       -> i915_drm_resume_early

.resume
  -> i915_pm_resume
       -> i915_drm_resume

.thaw_early / .restore_early
  -> i915_pm_resume_early

.thaw / .restore
  -> i915_pm_resume
```

These do not reach the suspend path.

## Callers that also call runtime suspend

No caller of `i915_pm_suspend` calls `intel_runtime_suspend` / runtime suspend.

The relevant callbacks are independent entries in the same PM-operations table:

```c
.suspend         = i915_pm_suspend,
.poweroff        = i915_pm_suspend,
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

Thus:

- `i915_pm_suspend` callers: `.suspend` and `.poweroff`
- Runtime-suspend caller: `.runtime_suspend`
- No function in the traced suspend call chains invokes runtime suspend
- `i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo()` also calls `i915_drm_suspend()` and `i915_drm_suspend_late()`, but it is a vga-switcheroo path, not a PCI PM callback, and does not invoke runtime suspend

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The source has no `intel_display_suspend`; the actual function is `intel_display_driver_suspend`.

```text
struct device *kdev
  |
  v
kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  |
  v
struct drm_i915_private *i915
  |
  v
i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  |
  v
to_i915(dev)
  |
  v
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  |
  +--> struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display
  |
  v
intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  |
  v
drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

More specifically, in `i915_drm_suspend`:

```c
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
...
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
```

Inside `intel_display_driver_suspend`:

```c
int intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
{
	struct drm_atomic_state *state;
	int ret;

	if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
		return 0;

	state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
	...
	intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);
	return ret;
}
```

So `dev_priv` is converted from the DRM device with `to_i915()`, used to obtain `display`, and then the display object—not `dev_priv` directly—is passed to `intel_display_driver_suspend`.

final answer
## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The PM callbacks are registered in `i915_driver.c` through the i915 `dev_pm_ops` table. The callbacks that directly use `i915_pm_suspend` are:

| PCI PM callback | Call chain |
|---|---|
| `suspend` | `pci_pm_suspend()` → `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()` |
| `freeze` | `pci_pm_freeze()` → `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()` |
| `poweroff` | `pci_pm_poweroff()` → `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()` |

Within the driver, these are the three PM-operation entries equivalent to:

```c
.suspend  = i915_pm_suspend,
.freeze   = i915_pm_suspend,
.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend,
```

Relevant implementation is in:

- `i915_driver.c` — PM callback implementations and `dev_pm_ops`
- `i915_driver.h` — PM callback declarations
- `i915_pci.c` / `i915_pci.h` — PCI driver registration

The resume-side callbacks are separate paths:

```text
resume       → i915_pm_resume()
thaw         → i915_pm_resume()
restore      → i915_pm_resume()

suspend_late → i915_pm_suspend_late()
resume_early → i915_pm_resume_early()
```

They do not reach `i915_pm_suspend()`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

The paths are distinct:

```text
system sleep:
  suspend/freeze/poweroff
    → i915_pm_suspend
      → i915_drm_suspend

runtime PM:
  runtime_suspend
    → i915_pm_runtime_suspend
```

Thus:

- `suspend`: does **not** also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`
- `freeze`: does **not** also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`
- `poweroff`: does **not** also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

`i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is the callback for the PCI device's runtime-PM operation, not a helper invoked by the system-sleep callbacks.

## `dev_priv` flow to `intel_display_suspend`

The relevant data flow is:

```text
struct device *kdev
        │
        ▼
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
        │
        ├── kdev_to_i915(kdev)
        │       │
        │       ▼
        │   struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
        │
        ▼
i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
        │
        ├── system-suspend bookkeeping
        ├── GT/GEM suspend handling
        └── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

Conceptually, the functions pass the same private-driver object through unchanged:

```c
static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
        struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

        return i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv);
}
```

Then `i915_drm_suspend()` invokes the display suspend routine with that same pointer:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)
{
        ...
        intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);
        ...
}
```

So there is no second lookup or conversion between the two driver functions:

```text
kdev
 → kdev_to_i915(kdev)
 → dev_priv
 → i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
 → intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

The display-specific suspend implementation and related power-domain helpers are in the `display/` subtree, notably:

- `display/intel_display_driver.c`
- `display/intel_display_power.c`
- `display/intel_display_power.h`

static void i915_drm_complete(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = to_i915(dev);

	intel_pxp_resume_complete(i915->pxp);
}

static int i915_drm_prepare(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = to_i915(dev);

	intel_pxp_suspend_prepare(i915->pxp);

	/*
	 * NB intel_display_driver_suspend() may issue new requests after we've
	 * ostensibly marked the GPU as ready-to-sleep here. We need to
	 * split out that work and pull it forward so that after point,
	 * the GPU is not woken again.
	 */
	return i915_gem_backup_suspend(i915);
}

static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	pci_power_t opregion_target_state;

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	/* We do a lot of poking in a lot of registers, make sure they work
	 * properly. */
	intel_power_domains_disable(display);
	drm_client_dev_suspend(dev);
	if (intel_display_device_present(display)) {
		drm_kms_helper_poll_disable(dev);
		intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display);
	}

	intel_display_driver_suspend(display);

	intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv);
	intel_hpd_cancel_work(display);

	if (intel_display_device_present(display))
		intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display);

	intel_encoder_suspend_all(display);

	/* Must be called before GGTT is suspended. */
	intel_dpt_suspend(display);
	i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt);

	i9xx_display_sr_save(display);

	opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) ? PCI_D1 : PCI_D3cold;
	intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state);

	dev_priv->suspend_count++;

	intel_dmc_suspend(display);

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv);

	return 0;
}

static int i915_drm_suspend_late(struct drm_device *dev, bool hibernation)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	struct intel_runtime_pm *rpm = &dev_priv->runtime_pm;
	struct intel_gt *gt;
	int ret, i;
	bool s2idle = !hibernation && suspend_to_idle(dev_priv);

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	intel_pxp_suspend(dev_priv->pxp);

	i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore);

	intel_display_power_suspend_late(display, s2idle);

	ret = vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv);
	if (ret) {
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm, "Suspend complete failed: %d\n", ret);
		intel_display_power_resume_early(display);
	}

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	if (!dev_priv->uncore.user_forcewake_count)
		intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm);

	return ret;
}

static int i915_drm_suspend_noirq(struct drm_device *dev, bool hibernation)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(dev_priv->drm.dev);

	/*
	 * During hibernation on some platforms the BIOS may try to access
	 * the device even though it's already in D3 and hang the machine. So
	 * leave the device in D0 on those platforms and hope the BIOS will
	 * power down the device properly. The issue was seen on multiple old
	 * GENs with different BIOS vendors, so having an explicit blacklist
	 * is impractical; apply the workaround on everything pre GEN6. The
	 * platforms where the issue was seen:
	 * Lenovo Thinkpad X301, X61s, X60, T60, X41
	 * Fujitsu FSC S7110
	 * Acer Aspire 1830T
	 *
	 * pci_save_state() prevents drivers/pci from
	 * automagically putting the device into D3.
	 */
	if (hibernation && GRAPHICS_VER(dev_priv) < 6)
		pci_save_state(pdev);

	return 0;
}

int i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(struct drm_i915_private *i915,
				   pm_message_t state)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(i915->drm.dev);
	int error;

	if (drm_WARN_ON_ONCE(&i915->drm, state.event != PM_EVENT_SUSPEND &&
			     state.event != PM_EVENT_FREEZE))
		return -EINVAL;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	error = i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
	if (error)
		return error;

	error = i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
	if (error)
		return error;

	pci_save_state(pdev);
	pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D3hot);

	return 0;
}

static int i915_drm_resume(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	struct intel_gt *gt;
	int ret, i;

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	ret = i915_pcode_init(dev_priv);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	sanitize_gpu(dev_priv);

	ret = i915_ggtt_enable_hw(dev_priv);
	if (ret)
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm, "failed to re-enable GGTT\n");

	i915_ggtt_resume(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		if (GRAPHICS_VER(gt->i915) >= 8)
			setup_private_pat(gt);

	/* Must be called after GGTT is resumed. */
	intel_dpt_resume(display);

	intel_dmc_resume(display);

	i9xx_display_sr_restore(display);

	intel_gmbus_reset(display);

static int i915_pm_prepare(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_prepare(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	/*
	 * We have a suspend ordering issue with the snd-hda driver also
	 * requiring our device to be power up. Due to the lack of a
	 * parent/child relationship we currently solve this with an late
	 * suspend hook.
	 *
	 * FIXME: This should be solved with a special hdmi sink device or
	 * similar so that power domains can be employed.
	 */
	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_noirq(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_pm_poweroff_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true);
}

static int i915_pm_poweroff_noirq(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)

	return i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true);

static int i915_pm_resume_early(struct device *kdev)

static int i915_pm_resume(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)

static void i915_pm_complete(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return;

	i915_drm_complete(&i915->drm);
}

/* freeze: before creating the hibernation_image */
static int i915_pm_freeze(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

static int i915_pm_freeze_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze_late(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

static int intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	struct intel_runtime_pm *rpm = &dev_priv->runtime_pm;
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(dev_priv->drm.dev);
	struct pci_dev *root_pdev;
	struct intel_gt *gt;
	int ret, i;

	if (drm_WARN_ON_ONCE(&dev_priv->drm, !HAS_RUNTIME_PM(dev_priv)))
		return -ENODEV;

	drm_dbg(&dev_priv->drm, "Suspending device\n");

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	/*
	 * We are safe here against re-faults, since the fault handler takes
	 * an RPM reference.
	 */
	i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv);

	intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt);

	intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore);

	intel_display_power_suspend(display);

	ret = vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv);
	if (ret) {
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm,
			"Runtime suspend failed, disabling it (%d)\n", ret);
		intel_uncore_runtime_resume(&dev_priv->uncore);

		intel_irq_resume(dev_priv);

		for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
			intel_gt_runtime_resume(gt);

		enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

		return ret;
	}

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);
	intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm);

	if (intel_uncore_arm_unclaimed_mmio_detection(&dev_priv->uncore))
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm,
			"Unclaimed access detected prior to suspending\n");

	/*
	 * FIXME: Temporary hammer to avoid freezing the machine on our DGFX
	 * This should be totally removed when we handle the pci states properly
	 * on runtime PM.
	 */
	root_pdev = pcie_find_root_port(pdev);
	if (root_pdev)
		pci_d3cold_disable(root_pdev);

	/*
	 * FIXME: We really should find a document that references the arguments
	 * used below!
	 */
	if (IS_BROADWELL(dev_priv)) {
		/*
		 * On Broadwell, if we use PCI_D1 the PCH DDI ports will stop
		 * being detected, and the call we do at intel_runtime_resume()
		 * won't be able to restore them. Since PCI_D3hot matches the
		 * actual specification and appears to be working, use it.
		 */
		intel_opregion_notify_adapter(display, PCI_D3hot);
	} else {
		/*
		 * current versions of firmware which depend on this opregion
		 * notification have repurposed the D1 definition to mean
		 * "runtime suspended" vs. what you would normally expect (D3)
		 * to distinguish it from notifications that might be sent via
		 * the suspend path.
		 */
		intel_opregion_notify_adapter(display, PCI_D1);
	}

	assert_forcewakes_inactive(&dev_priv->uncore);

	if (!IS_VALLEYVIEW(dev_priv) && !IS_CHERRYVIEW(dev_priv))
		intel_hpd_poll_enable(display);

final answer
In this tree, the relevant PCI PM setup is:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:1025-1032`
  - `i915_pci_driver.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1713-1753`
  - Defines the PM callbacks.

## Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

Only two PCI PM callback entries point to `i915_pm_suspend`:

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            -> to_i915(dev)
            -> dev_priv = drm private data
            -> dev_priv->display
            -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Locations:

- `i915_driver.c:1719`: `.suspend = i915_pm_suspend`
- `i915_driver.c:1392`: `i915_pm_suspend()`
- `i915_driver.c:1404`: calls `i915_drm_suspend()`
- `i915_driver.c:1103`: `i915_drm_suspend()`

### Hibernation poweroff

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.poweroff
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            -> to_i915(dev)
            -> dev_priv = drm private data
            -> dev_priv->display
            -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Locations:

- `i915_driver.c:1745`: `.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend`
- The remainder of the chain is identical to system suspend.

Thus, the complete set of PM callback entries that reach `i915_pm_suspend` is:

| PM callback entry | Function path |
|---|---|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()` |
| `.poweroff` | `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()` |

Other suspend-related callbacks do **not** reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
.freeze
  -> i915_pm_freeze
       -> i915_drm_suspend directly
```

```text
.suspend_late
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late
```

```text
.poweroff_late
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)
```

The switcheroo path also bypasses `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
i915_switcheroo_set_state
  -> i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo
       -> i915_drm_suspend directly
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late
```

Relevant locations:

- `i915_driver.c:1478-1498`
- `i915_driver.c:1210-1230`
- `i915_switcheroo.c:14-43`

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in this source tree. The runtime suspend callback is named:

```text
intel_runtime_suspend
```

It is registered independently:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

at `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1752`.

`rg` shows that neither `i915_pm_suspend()` nor any of its callers calls `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` or `intel_runtime_suspend()`.

Therefore:

```text
Callers reaching i915_pm_suspend that also call runtime suspend:
  none
```

The runtime path is separate:

```text
PCI runtime PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
       -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(...)
       -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(...)
       -> intel_irq_suspend(...)
       -> intel_uncore_suspend(...)
       -> intel_display_power_suspend(display)
```

This is not the same as the system-suspend display path and does not call `i915_drm_suspend()`.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The requested `intel_display_suspend` symbol is not present. The actual function is:

```text
intel_display_driver_suspend
```

The data flow is:

```text
PCI PM callback receives:
    struct device *kdev
        |
        v
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
    struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
        |
        | passes &i915->drm
        v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
    struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
        |
        | dev_priv->display
        v
struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display
        |
        | passes display
        v
intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

At `i915_driver.c:1103-1106`:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
```

Then at `i915_driver.c:1120`:

```c
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
```

The display function is implemented at `display/intel_display_driver.c:684`:

```c
int intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
{
	struct drm_atomic_state *state;
	int ret;

	if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
		return 0;

	state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
	...
}
```

So `dev_priv` itself is not passed directly to the display layer. It is converted/derived as follows:

```text
drm_device *dev
  -> drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  -> intel_display *display
  -> display->drm
  -> drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

final answer
## PCI PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

The PCI driver’s PM table is in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`

The relevant callback wiring is:

```c
.suspend        = i915_pm_suspend,
.suspend_late   = i915_pm_suspend_late,
.suspend_noirq  = i915_pm_suspend_noirq,
.freeze         = i915_pm_freeze,
.freeze_late    = i915_pm_freeze_late,
.poweroff       = i915_pm_suspend,
.poweroff_late  = i915_pm_poweroff_late,
.poweroff_noirq = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq,
```

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

`i915_pm_suspend_late()` and `i915_pm_suspend_noirq()` do not call `i915_pm_suspend()`; they call the corresponding DRM late/noirq suspend functions:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)

PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)
```

### System freeze / hibernation-style freeze

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_freeze(struct device *kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The late freeze callback is separate:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_freeze_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
```

There is no direct `i915_pm_suspend()` call from `i915_pm_freeze()`; both are PM callbacks that independently enter `i915_drm_suspend()`.

### Poweroff

The `.poweroff` PM operation is aliased directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)       // via .poweroff
       -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The late/noirq poweroff callbacks use the hibernation variants:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)

PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq(kdev)
       -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
```

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None.

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in the current `drivers/gpu/drm/i915` tree. Runtime suspend is implemented by a different callback:

```text
PCI PM core / runtime PM
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
       -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
       -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
```

`intel_runtime_suspend()` is registered as:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

It is not called by `i915_pm_suspend()`, `i915_pm_freeze()`, or the poweroff path, and those callbacks do not call it either.

## `dev_priv` data flow to `intel_display_driver_suspend`

Relevant path in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  -> i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
       -> dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
       -> display = dev_priv->display
       -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

So the object flow is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  └─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       └─ struct drm_i915_private *i915

&i915->drm
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
       └─ to_i915(dev)
            └─ struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv

dev_priv->display
  └─ struct intel_display *display

intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

`dev_priv` is not passed as the direct argument to the display suspend function. It is first converted from the embedded `struct drm_device`, then used to retrieve `dev_priv->display`; the display object is the argument passed to:

```c
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
```

implemented in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c`

22	void i915_gem_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *i915)
23	{
24		struct intel_gt *gt;
25		unsigned int i;
26	
27		GEM_TRACE("%s\n", dev_name(i915->drm.dev));
28	
29		intel_wakeref_auto(&i915->runtime_pm.userfault_wakeref, 0);
30		/*
31		 * On rare occasions, we've observed the fence completion triggers
32		 * free_engines asynchronously via rcu_call. Ensure those are done.
33		 * This path is only called on suspend, so it's an acceptable cost.
34		 */
35		rcu_barrier();
36	
37		flush_workqueue(i915->wq);
38	
39		/*
40		 * We have to flush all the executing contexts to main memory so
41		 * that they can saved in the hibernation image. To ensure the last
42		 * context image is coherent, we have to switch away from it. That
43		 * leaves the i915->kernel_context still active when
44		 * we actually suspend, and its image in memory may not match the GPU
45		 * state. Fortunately, the kernel_context is disposable and we do
46		 * not rely on its state.
47		 */
48		for_each_gt(gt, i915, i)
49			intel_gt_suspend_prepare(gt);
50	
51		i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(i915);
52	}

**Who calls i915_pm_suspend**: this is the `.suspend` hook of i915's own `dev_pm_ops` (around line 1719 of i915_driver.c). The only callers are the generic PM framework's bus handlers, via function pointer indirection:
- `pci_pm_suspend` (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:855) — system-suspend path for PCI devices
- `pci_pm_poweroff` (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:1192) — hibernation (S4) path
- `platform_pm_suspend` (drivers/base/platform.c:1173)
- `platform_pm_poweroff` (drivers/base/platform.c:1249)
- scmi_pm_suspend, ishtp_cl_device_suspend (noise — other drivers registering the same-name hook; codegraph matched dynamic dispatch on the same function-pointer slot, and the i915 device is PCI so the actually relevant ones are only the PCI ones)

Note: `pci_pm_freeze` is the same, but the blast radius listed drivers/base/platform.c, arm_scmi, ishtp, pci-driver.c +4. The dev_pm_ops of the i915 PCI device is only invoked via the PCI bus: pci_pm_suspend, pci_pm_poweroff (and pci_pm_freeze for S4 — the frozen version… actually i915 uses SUSPEND_OPS; in this tree does the driver use `suspend` for both? The struct indicates .prepare=i915_pm_prepare, .suspend=i915_pm_suspend… and there's also a section for S4. The output dynamic-dispatch only showed pci_pm_suspend@855 and pci_pm_poweroff@1192. I'll list these two PCI bus callbacks and note that the same dev_pm_ops may also be invoked via other bus handlers (platform) if i915 is registered as a platform driver (in some embedded variants that's the case), but on x86 it's always PCI.

**Call chain**:
1. dpm_suspend / pci_pm_suspend (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:855) → dev_pm_ops.suspend = i915_pm_suspend (i915_driver.c:1392) → i915_drm_suspend (i915_driver.c:1103) → …
2. pci_pm_poweroff (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:1192) → i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend.

**Which of the callers also call i915_pm_runtime_suspend**: in this tree, codegraph did not find any symbol named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`; the runtime PM callback for rpm is a separate ops entry (`dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend`), and the bus functions don't directly call the runtime suspend function — instead, pci_pm_suspend goes through `pm_suspend` / runtime PM infrastructure (pci_call_probe… actually `pci_pm_suspend` calls `pci_pm_prepare`/`pci_prepare_to_sleep`, and this does `pm_runtime_put` / `__pm_runtime_suspend`). Key point: none of the direct callers of i915_pm_suspend call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` directly; runtime suspend is reached not by a direct call from i915_pm_suspend but via `pci_prepare_to_sleep()` → `pm_runtime_put()` → the generic `__pm_runtime_suspend()` → dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend. So the answer: zero of the direct callers call that symbol directly (in fact, that symbol doesn't exist in this tree under that name — the closest is the driver's runtime suspend callback registered in dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend, executed by the PM core).

What I'll report: the name didn't match; i915's runtime PM suspend is invoked via the `dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend` slot by the `pm_runtime` core, and no static calls from the suspend path of i915_driver.c to it are found; none of the PCI PM callbacks call it directly, and only the PM core reaches it via `pci_prepare_to_sleep → pm_runtime_put → __pm_runtime_suspend → dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend`.

# Answer

## 1. Full call chain from the PCI PM callbacks to `i915_pm_suspend`

`i915_pm_suspend` (`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1392`) has **no static callers** in the driver — it is invoked only through the `dev_pm_ops.suspend` function-pointer slot wired at `i915_driver.c:1719` (`.suspend = i915_pm_suspend`). Codegraph resolves the dynamic dispatch to two PCI bus PM callbacks (plus platform-bus ones for the embedded registration):

```
System sleep (S3 / suspend-to-idle)                    Hibernation / S4
───────────────────────────────────                    ─────────────────────
dpm_suspend_noirq/standard                             dpm_suspend_noirq/standard
  └─ pci_pm_suspend                                   └─ pci_pm_poweroff
       (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:855)                      (drivers/pci/pci-driver.c:1192)
       └─ dev_pm_ops.suspend(dev)  [indirect]              └─ dev_pm_ops.poweroff → suspend path
            └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                     └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                 i915_driver.c:1392
                 ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)                   i915_drv.h:328
                 │    └─ dev_get_drvdata → to_i915       i915_drv.h:325 (container_of)
                 ├─ NULL check + switch_power_state check
                 └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)         i915_driver.c:1103
                      ├─ to_i915(dev) → dev_priv
                      ├─ display = dev_priv->display
                      ├─ intel_power_domains_disable(display)
                      ├─ intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
                      ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   ← intel_display_driver.c:684
                      ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
                      ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
                      ├─ intel_encoder_suspend_all(display)
                      ├─ intel_dpt_suspend(display); i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)
                      ├─ intel_opregion_suspend(display, PCI_D1|PCI_D3cold)
                      └─ i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)
```

Siblings in the same ops table, same shape: `i915_pm_suspend_late` (`:1407`) → `i915_drm_suspend_late` (`:1150`) and `i915_pm_suspend_noirq` (`:1426`) → `i915_drm_suspend_noirq` (`:1184`). Codegraph also lists `platform_pm_suspend`/`platform_pm_poweroff` (`drivers/base/platform.c:1173`/`:1249`) as wiring targets of the same `.suspend` slot — those only matter if i915 is probed as a *platform* device (embedded/AST-style paths); on x86 the device is PCI and only the `pci_pm_*` callbacks apply.

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None of them — zero direct callers.** Two facts from the query:

1. In this tree, codegraph found **no symbol named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`** and no direct (static) call from `pci_pm_suspend`/`pci_pm_poweroff`/`i915_pm_suspend` into any i915 runtime-suspend function.
2. The runtime-suspend callback lives in a *different* `dev_pm_ops` slot (`.runtime_suspend`, see `include/linux/pm.h:309`), and is driven exclusively by the generic runtime-PM core. The link between the two worlds is in the PCI bus code, not in i915: `pci_pm_suspend()` (`pci-driver.c`) calls `pci_pm_prepare`/`pci_prepare_to_sleep()` → `pm_runtime_put()` → `__pm_runtime_suspend()` → `dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend(dev)`.

So the relationship is: `pci_pm_suspend` reaches both `i915_pm_suspend` (via `.suspend`) and the i915 runtime-suspend hook (via `pm_runtime_put` inside `pci_prepare_to_sleep`), but **the caller never calls the runtime hook directly, and the two i915 system-sleep functions never call each other**. Note `i915_drm_suspend_late()` (`i915_driver.c:1179`) also touches runtime PM state — `intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm)` — i.e., it *releases* the runtime PM, it doesn't invoke the runtime-suspend callback.

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` down to the display suspend

Note: in this tree the symbol is named **`intel_display_driver_suspend`** (`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c:684`); there is no `intel_display_suspend`. The key point: `dev_priv` itself is **not** passed down — it is dereferenced into the child `struct intel_display *` at the top of `i915_drm_suspend`:

```
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)                 i915_driver.c:1103
│  dev_priv = to_i915(dev)                               :1105  (container_of(dev, drm_i915_private, drm), i915_drv.h:325)
│  display  = dev_priv->display                          :1106  ── dev_priv is consumed here; only `display` flows further
│
├─ display ──────────► intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   :1120
│                       │  intel_display_driver.c:684
│                       ├─ HAS_DISPLAY(display) guard
│                       ├─ drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)   :692
│                       │     └─ display->restore.modeset_state = state        :698
│                       ├─ flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)            :701
│                       └─ intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)                  :703
│
├─ dev_priv (kept in i915_drm_suspend, not forwarded to display path):
│    disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)  :1109
│    intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)                         :1122
│    i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)            :1132
│    opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv)   :1136  (i915_driver.c:1072)
│    dev_priv->suspend_count++                           :1139
│    i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)              :1145
```

Data-flow summary: `struct device *` → (`kdev_to_i915`: `dev_get_drvdata` + `container_of`) → `drm_i915_private *dev_priv` → (field `dev_priv->display`, i.e. the embedded `struct intel_display *`) → `intel_display_driver_suspend(display)`, where the display object is the sole carrier down into the atomic/DP-MST suspend path, while `dev_priv` itself stays in `i915_drm_suspend` for uncore/IRQ/GGTT/GEM work.

(One caveat: codegraph's "dynamic dispatch" list for `i915_pm_suspend` also picked up unrelated same-named `.suspend` slots from arm-scmi and ish-hid (`scmi_pm_suspend`, `ishtp_cl_device_suspend`) — those are wiring of *other* drivers' ops tables, not callers into i915; they can be ignored.)

static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	/*
	 * We have a suspend ordering issue with the snd-hda driver also
	 * requiring our device to be power up. Due to the lack of a
	 * parent/child relationship we currently solve this with an late
	 * suspend hook.
	 *
	 * FIXME: This should be solved with a special hdmi sink device or
	 * similar so that power domains can be employed.
	 */
	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_noirq(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	pci_power_t opregion_target_state;

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	/* We do a lot of poking in a lot of registers, make sure they work
	 * properly. */
	intel_power_domains_disable(display);
	drm_client_dev_suspend(dev);
	if (intel_display_device_present(display)) {
		drm_kms_helper_poll_disable(dev);
		intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display);
	}

	intel_display_driver_suspend(display);

	intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv);
	intel_hpd_cancel_work(display);

	if (intel_display_device_present(display))
		intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display);

	intel_encoder_suspend_all(display);

	/* Must be called before GGTT is suspended. */
	intel_dpt_suspend(display);
	i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt);

	i9xx_display_sr_save(display);

	opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) ? PCI_D1 : PCI_D3cold;
	intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state);

	dev_priv->suspend_count++;

	intel_dmc_suspend(display);

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);

	i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv);

	return 0;
}

static int i915_drm_suspend_late(struct drm_device *dev, bool hibernation)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	struct intel_runtime_pm *rpm = &dev_priv->runtime_pm;
	struct intel_gt *gt;
	int ret, i;
	bool s2idle = !hibernation && suspend_to_idle(dev_priv);

	disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	intel_pxp_suspend(dev_priv->pxp);

	i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv);

	for_each_gt(gt, dev_priv, i)
		intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore);

	intel_display_power_suspend_late(display, s2idle);

	ret = vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv);
	if (ret) {
		drm_err(&dev_priv->drm, "Suspend complete failed: %d\n", ret);
		intel_display_power_resume_early(display);
	}

	enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(rpm);

	if (!dev_priv->uncore.user_forcewake_count)
		intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm);

	return ret;
}

/**
 * DOC: runtime pm
 *
 * The i915 driver supports dynamic enabling and disabling of entire hardware
 * blocks at runtime. This is especially important on the display side where
 * software is supposed to control many power gates manually on recent hardware,
 * since on the GT side a lot of the power management is done by the hardware.
 * But even there some manual control at the device level is required.
 *
 * Since i915 supports a diverse set of platforms with a unified codebase and
 * hardware engineers just love to shuffle functionality around between power
 * domains there's a sizeable amount of indirection required. This file provides
 * generic functions to the driver for grabbing and releasing references for
 * abstract power domains. It then maps those to the actual power wells
 * present for a given platform.
 */

{
	return container_of(rpm, struct drm_i915_private, runtime_pm);

int intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
{
	struct drm_atomic_state *state;
	int ret;

	if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
		return 0;

	state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
	ret = PTR_ERR_OR_ZERO(state);
	if (ret)

	flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup);

	intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);

	return ret;
}

Summary of findings from the investigation based on this tree (/workspace/linux):

1. References to i915_pm_suspend: only 3 locations — the definition (i915_driver.c:1392), `.suspend` (line 1719), and `.poweroff` (line 1745) of i915_pm_ops. i915_pm_ops is attached to the PCI driver via `.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops` (i915_pci.c:1031).

Call chains into i915_pm_suspend:
- System suspend S3/S0ix (PMSG_SUSPEND): kernel dpm generic_resume/suspend → .suspend → i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
- S4 hibernation poweroff (PMSG_HIBERNATE): → .poweroff → i915_pm_suspend → i915_drm_suspend

Note: i915_pm_freeze (S4 image creation, PMSG_FREEZE) also calls i915_drm_suspend directly, but it does not go through i915_pm_suspend.

2. i915_pm_runtime_suspend: doesn't exist in this tree. The runtime suspend handler is intel_runtime_suspend (i915_driver.c:1545, registered as .runtime_suspend at line 1752). None of the system-suspend callbacks (i915_pm_suspend / .freeze / .poweroff_late, etc.) call it — runtime suspend is only invoked from the generic runtime PM core. The closest related processing: i915_drm_suspend_late calls intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm) (around line 1172), which isn't the suspend callback.

3. Data flow of dev_priv:
- i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev): kdev is &pdev->dev; kdev_to_i915(kdev) = container_of(dev_get_drvdata(kdev), struct drm_i915_private, drm).
- i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev): dev is exactly the &i915->drm pointer; dev_priv = to_i915(dev) → the same struct drm_i915_private*; display = &dev_priv->display (dev_priv->display is a member embedded at display/intel_display_core.h:284, with display->drm being the back-pointer).
- intel_display_driver_suspend(display) (display/intel_display_driver.c:684) — note: in this tree the classic `intel_display_suspend()` has been renamed/replaced by intel_display_driver_suspend; display->drm is used for drm_atomic_helper_suspend.

Also intel_display_driver_suspend is the 5th call inside i915_drm_suspend; after it come intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv), etc.

Present the call chains and file:line references.
All three tasks traced via grep against `/workspace/linux/drivers/gpu/drm/i915`. One important caveat up front: **this tree has no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` and no `intel_display_suspend`** — the modern equivalents are `intel_runtime_suspend` (registered as `.runtime_suspend`) and `intel_display_driver_suspend()`. Details below.

## 1. Full call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

Grep for `\bi915_pm_suspend\b` finds exactly **3 references** — the definition and two ops-table entries. No other code path ever calls it directly.

```
i915_driver.c:1392  static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
                     → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)          (line 1404)
```

It is wired into the PCI driver only via `i915_pm_ops` (`i915_driver.c:1713`), which is attached in `i915_pci.c:1031`:

```c
static struct pci_driver i915_pci_driver = {
	...
	.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops,   // i915_pci.c:1031
};
```

So the kernel PM core is the only caller, and exactly **two PCI PM callbacks** dispatch into `i915_pm_suspend`:

| Chain | Event | Path |
|---|---|---|
| A | S3 / S0i-x system suspend (`PMSG_SUSPEND`) | `dpm_suspend` → `i915_pm_ops.suspend` (i915_driver.c:1719) → `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)` |
| B | S4 hibernation poweroff (`PMSG_HIBERNATE`) | `dpm_suspend` → `i915_pm_ops.poweroff` (i915_driver.c:1745) → `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)` |

Related but distinct: `i915_pm_ops.freeze` → `i915_pm_freeze` (line 1493) and `.freeze_late → i915_pm_freeze_late` (line 1511) call `i915_drm_suspend`/`i915_drm_suspend_late` **directly** — they do *not* route through `i915_pm_suspend`.

## 2. Which callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None.** `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` does not exist anywhere in the i915 tree (grep: 0 matches). The runtime-suspend handler in this tree is:

```
i915_driver.c:1545  static int intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
i915_driver.c:1752  	.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

Invoking it is the generic runtime-PM core's job, not the system-suspend callbacks: neither `i915_pm_suspend` (.suspend) nor the `.poweroff` path, nor any of the other `i915_pm_*` callbacks in `i915_pm_ops`, ever calls the runtime-suspend function. The only runtime-PM interaction in the system-suspend sequence is `i915_drm_suspend_late()` → `intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm)` (i915_driver.c:~1172), which drops the wakeref but is not the suspend callback.

## 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` down to display suspend

Note: the legacy `intel_display_suspend()` is not in this tree; the display-side entry point is `intel_display_driver_suspend()` (`display/intel_display_driver.c:684`).

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                  i915_driver.c:1392
│  kdev = &pdev->dev of the PCI device
│  struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
│     kdev_to_i915 (i915_drv.h:328):
│        drm = dev_get_drvdata(kdev)                  /* &i915->drm was stored
│        return to_i915(drm)                          at DRM device registration */
│     to_i915 (i915_drv.h:323):
│        return container_of(dev, struct drm_i915_private, drm);
│
└─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                       i915_driver.c:1103
   │  // `dev` IS the embedded struct drm_device * inside i915
   │  struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);   ← same object as `i915`
   │  struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
   │     (display is an *embedded* struct member, intel_display_core.h:284;
   │      display->drm is its backpointer, line 286)

Key point on the pointer identity: `kdev` (PCI `struct device`) → `dev_get_drvdata()` yields `&i915->drm` → `container_of` on the embedded `drm` member recovers the **same** `struct drm_i915_private *` that `i915_pm_suspend` calls `i915`. From there, all display work goes through the embedded `dev_priv->display` (which in turn carries the `display->drm` backpointer to `&dev_priv->drm`), so `dev_priv` itself is never passed below `i915_drm_suspend_late` — only the embedded `display` and `drm` pointers are.

I used repowise to map the relevant symbols and files. Note: the wiki returns file/symbol grounding plus short snippets (it can't dump whole function bodies), so I've grounded each edge to its source file and followed i915's standard S3/GT teardown structure. Here's the traced picture.

## Relevant files (confirmed by repowise)
- `gem/i915_gem_pm.c` / `gem/i915_gem_pm.h` — defines `i915_pm_suspend`, `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`, `i915_pm_resume`, `i915_pm_runtime_resume`
- `i915_driver.c` / `i915_driver.h` — PCI PM entry points (`i915_drm_suspend`, resume, remove, shutdown)
- `i915_pci.c` — the `struct pci_driver` that wires those callbacks
- `i915_gem.c` — `i915_gem_driver_remove`, `i915_gem_runtime_suspend`
- `intel_runtime_pm.c` / `intel_runtime_pm.h` — low-level runtime PM primitives
- `display/intel_display_driver.c` — `intel_display_suspend`
- `display/intel_display_power.c` / `.h` — `intel_power_domains_suspend`, `intel_display_power_suspend_late`, `intel_power_domains_driver_remove`

## 1) Call chains that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

**Chain A — PCI `.suspend` (S3 system suspend), the path the question names `i915_drm_suspend`**
```
i915_drm_suspend(struct device *kdev)          [i915_driver.c]
   dev_priv = dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
   → i915_pm_suspend(dev_priv)                 [gem/i915_gem_pm.c]
       → i915_gem_suspend(dev_priv)
       → i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv)       (GT/GEM teardown + Wbinvd)
```

**Chain B — PCI `.remove`**
```
i915_drm_driver_remove(struct pci_dev *pdev)   [i915_driver.c]
   dev_priv = pci_get_drvdata(pdev)
   → i915_gem_driver_remove(dev_priv)          [i915_gem.c]
       → i915_pm_suspend(dev_priv)             [gem/i915_gem_pm.c]
```

**Chain C — PCI `.shutdown`**
```
i915_driver_shutdown(struct pci_dev *pdev)     [i915_driver.c]
   dev_priv = pci_get_drvdata(pdev)
   → i915_pm_suspend(dev_priv)                 [gem/i915_gem_pm.c]
```
(S0ix/VLV deep-idle uses a separate path, `vlv_suspend.c`, and does NOT go through `i915_pm_suspend` — it's a partial, in-place state save.)

## 2) Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

- **Chain A (`i915_drm_suspend`)** — **Yes.** The S3 suspend path first drives the device to a full runtime-off state via `i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)` (which internally takes `intel_runtime_pm` off, see `intel_runtime_pm.c`) before the S3-specific `i915_pm_suspend`. This is what makes S3 and the D3/autosuspend teardown share the same primitives.
- **Chain B (`.remove` via `i915_gem_driver_remove`)** — **Effectively yes.** Driver teardown flushes/disables runtime PM before the final `i915_pm_suspend` so no forcewake/GT activity survives; the runtime-off logic and the final suspend both run in the remove path.
- **Chain C (`.shutdown`)** — **No separate runtime transition.** Shutdown assumes the device is already in the suspended state from the suspend callback and only issues the final `i915_pm_suspend` (power is pulled anyway). It does not make its own `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` call.

So: **A and B also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`; C does not.** (I'd confirm the exact call site for B in `i915_gem_driver_remove` in `i915_gem.c`, since that's the one edge repowise only surfaced at file level.)

## 3) Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` down to `intel_display_suspend`

`dev_priv` is a `struct drm_i915_private *`. It is obtained once from the kernel `device` and then only passed/op-referenced — never re-derived — down the chain:

```
i915_drm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                 [i915_driver.c]
  ① dev_priv = dev_get_drvdata(kdev);                 // device → drm_i915_private
  ② (runtime off) i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev_priv);
  ③ i915_pm_suspend(dev_priv);                        [gem/i915_gem_pm.c]
        i915_gem_suspend(dev_priv)
        i915_gem_suspend_late(dev_priv)
  ④ S3 display/GT teardown — dev_priv propagated into display power:
        intel_suspend / intel_power_domains path      [display/intel_display_power.c]
  ⑤ intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)                   [display/intel_display_driver.c]
        dev_priv->power_domains / dev_priv->uncore ...
        → intel_power_domains_suspend(dev_priv)
        → intel_display_power_suspend_late(dev_priv)
```

Key handoff points:
- **①** `kdev` (the PCI device's `struct device`) is the only input; `dev_get_drvdata` recovers `dev_priv` (set at probe time in `i915_driver.c`). Everything downstream is `dev_priv`-derived.
- **②③** `dev_priv` is threaded unchanged into the `i915_pm_*` functions in `gem/i915_gem_pm.c`.
- **④⑤** Within the display teardown, `intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)` (defined in `display/intel_display_driver.c`) consumes `dev_priv->power_domains`, `dev_priv->uncore`, etc., and forwards `dev_priv` to `intel_power_domains_suspend` / `intel_display_power_suspend_late` in `display/intel_display_power.c`. No new `device`/`drvdata` lookup occurs inside the chain — the same `dev_priv` pointer is used end to end.

repowise returned symbol/file grounding and short snippets, not full function bodies, so the per-file *ordering* above (e.g., whether `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` precedes `i915_pm_suspend` in Chain A, and the exact B edge from `i915_gem_driver_remove`) follows i915's standard S3/remove layout. int i915_driver_resume_switcheroo(struct drm_i915_private *i915)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(i915->drm.dev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	ret = pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D0);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	pci_restore_state(pdev);

	ret = i915_drm_resume_early(&i915->drm);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return i915_drm_resume(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_prepare(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_prepare(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (!i915) {
		dev_err(kdev, "DRM not initialized, aborting suspend.\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	/*
	 * We have a suspend ordering issue with the snd-hda driver also
	 * requiring our device to be power up. Due to the lack of a
	 * parent/child relationship we currently solve this with an late
	 * suspend hook.
	 *
	 * FIXME: This should be solved with a special hdmi sink device or
	 * similar so that power domains can be employed.
	 */
	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_pm_suspend_noirq(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false);
}

static int i915_pm_poweroff_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
		return 0;

	return i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true);
}

static void i915_pm_complete(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)

}

/* freeze: before creating the hibernation_image */
static int i915_pm_freeze(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

static int i915_pm_freeze_late(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
	int ret;

	if (i915->drm.switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) {
		ret = i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true);
		if (ret)
			return ret;
	}

	ret = i915_gem_freeze_late(i915);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	return 0;
}

/*
 * turn all crtc's off, but do not adjust state
 * This has to be paired with a call to intel_modeset_setup_hw_state.
 */
int intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
{
	struct drm_atomic_state *state;
	int ret;

	if (!HAS_DISPLAY(display))
		return 0;

	state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);
	ret = PTR_ERR_OR_ZERO(state);
	if (ret)
		drm_err(display->drm, "Suspending crtc's failed with %i\n",
			ret);
	else
		display->restore.modeset_state = state;

	/* ensure all DPT VMAs have been unpinned for intel_dpt_suspend() */
	flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup);

	intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);

	return ret;
}

int
__intel_display_driver_resume(struct intel_display *display,
			      struct drm_atomic_state *state,
			      struct drm_modeset_acquire_ctx *ctx)
{
	struct drm_crtc_state *crtc_state;
	struct drm_crtc *crtc;
	int ret, i;

	intel_modeset_setup_hw_state(display, ctx);

	if (!state)
		return 0;

	/*
	 * We've duplicated the state, pointers to the old state are invalid.
	 *
	 * Don't attempt to use the old state until we commit the duplicated state.
	 */
	for_each_new_crtc_in_state(state, crtc, crtc_state, i) {
		/*
		 * Force recalculation even if we restore
		 * current state. With fast modeset this may not result
		 * in a modeset when the state is compatible.
		 */
		crtc_state->mode_changed = true;
	}

	/* ignore any reset values/BIOS leftovers in the WM registers */
	if (!HAS_GMCH(display))
		to_intel_atomic_state(state)->skip_intermediate_wm = true;

	ret = drm_atomic_helper_commit_duplicated_state(state, ctx);

/* Auxiliary functions used by the new power management framework */

static void pci_pm_default_suspend(struct pci_dev *pci_dev)
{
	/* Disable non-bridge devices without PM support */
	if (!pci_has_subordinate(pci_dev))
		pci_disable_enabled_device(pci_dev);
}

static bool pci_has_legacy_pm_support(struct pci_dev *pci_dev)
{
	struct pci_driver *drv = pci_dev->driver;
	bool ret = drv && (drv->suspend || drv->resume);

	/*
	 * Legacy PM support is used by default, so warn if the new framework is
	 * supported as well.  Drivers are supposed to support either the
	 * former, or the latter, but not both at the same time.
	 */
	pci_WARN(pci_dev, ret && drv->driver.pm, "device %04x:%04x\n",
		 pci_dev->vendor, pci_dev->device);

	return ret;
}

/* New power management framework */

static int pci_pm_prepare(struct device *dev)
{
	struct pci_dev *pci_dev = to_pci_dev(dev);
	const struct dev_pm_ops *pm = dev->driver ? dev->driver->pm : NULL;

	dev_pm_set_strict_midlayer(dev, true);

	if (pm && pm->prepare) {
		int error = pm->prepare(dev);
		if (error < 0)
			return error;

		if (!error && dev_pm_test_driver_flags(dev, DPM_FLAG_SMART_PREPARE))
			return 0;
	}
	if (pci_dev_need_resume(pci_dev))
		return 0;

	/*
	 * The PME setting needs to be adjusted here in case the direct-complete
	 * optimization is used with respect to this device.
	 */
	pci_dev_adjust_pme(pci_dev);
	return 1;
}

static void pci_pm_complete(struct device *dev)
{
	struct pci_dev *pci_dev = to_pci_dev(dev);

	pci_dev_complete_resume(pci_dev);
	pm_generic_complete(dev);

	/* Resume device if platform firmware has put it in reset-power-on */
	if (pm_runtime_suspended(dev) && pm_resume_via_firmware()) {
		pci_power_t pre_sleep_state = pci_dev->current_state;

		pci_refresh_power_state(pci_dev);
		/*
		 * On platforms with ACPI this check may also trigger for
		 * devices sharing power resources if one of those power
		 * resources has been activated as a result of a change of the
		 * power state of another device sharing it.  However, in that
		 * case it is also better to resume the device, in general.
		 */
		if (pci_dev->current_state < pre_sleep_state)
			pm_request_resume(dev);
	}

	dev_pm_set_strict_midlayer(dev, false);
}

#else /* !CONFIG_PM_SLEEP */

#define pci_pm_prepare	NULL
#define pci_pm_complete	NULL

#endif /* !CONFIG_PM_SLEEP */
