## Verdict up front

The WARN is a **use-after-sysfs-removal / missing-reference bug in the Type-C class driver** (`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`), triggered from UCSI's connector-change work. The code in this tree is **still unguarded and identical to upstream v6.17** — **no fix is present in this tree**, and to my knowledge (through early 2026) **no fix has been merged upstream** for this exact warning.

---

## 1. Exact call chain (file:line for every hop)

| # | Function | Location | What it does |
|---|----------|----------|--------------|
| 1 | `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` | `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264` | Runs on `kworker` when UCSI PPM raises `CONNECT_CHANGE`; handles it at `ucsi.c:1306`; with `CONNECTED == 0` calls `ucsi_unregister_partner(con)` at `ucsi.c:1324-1326` |
| 2 | `ucsi_unregister_partner()` | `ucsi.c:1138-1154` | Guard is only `if (!con->partner) return;` (`ucsi.c:1140`), then calls `typec_unregister_partner(con->partner)` at `ucsi.c:1151` |
| 3 | `typec_unregister_partner()` | `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1196` | Takes `port->partner_link_lock` and, **unconditionally**, if `port->usb2_dev` (`class.c:1184`) / `port->usb3_dev` (`class.c:1188`) is non-NULL, calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:1185`, `1189`) |
| 4 | `typec_partner_unlink_device()` | `class.c:906-913` | **Offending function.** Calls `sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev))` (`class.c:908`) and `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` (`class.c:909`) with no check that the link/directory still exists |
| 5 | `sysfs_remove_link()` | `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-153` | `parent = kobj->sd;` then `kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name)` (`symlink.c:150-152`) |
| 6 | `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` | `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1752` | **The WARN site**: `if (!parent) { WARN(1, "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name); return -ENOENT; }` at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1730-1733` (line 1706 in your 6.17.0-1011-oem build, same branch, shifted by distro patches). Name `'typec'` proves the failing call is `class.c:909`, i.e. the parent is the **USB device's kobject**, and its `sd` was NULL. |

The corresponding create-side is `typec_partner_link_device()` (`class.c:888-904`): `sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec")` at `class.c:892`.

## 2. Why `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns` fails with ENOENT ("no directory")

The "no directory" WARN is only taken on the `!parent` branch — it is *not* "link not found" (that path at `dir.c:1739-1751` just returns `-ENOENT` silently). `parent` is `dev->kobj->sd`, and `sd` is NULLed by `kobject_cleanup()` (`drivers/base/core.c`) once the object's sysfs dir has been removed at device release. So the evidence is:

> The USB device stored in `port->usb2_dev`/`port->usb3_dev` **had already lost its sysfs directory when the UCSI work ran** — its whole `/sys/devices/.../typec` link vanished with the directory, yet `typec_partner_unlink_device()` still tried to remove the link by name from `dev->kobj`.

## 3. How the dangling state arises (root cause)

Three properties in `class.c` combine:

1. **Raw, non-refcounted pointers.** `typec_partner_attach()` (`class.c:2144-2167`) stores the USB device with a plain `port->usb2_dev = dev;` / `port->usb3_dev = dev;` (`class.c:2154`, `:2157`) — no `get_device()`. The typec class has no way to keep that USB `struct device` alive, so when the USB core deregisters the device, nothing in the typec world holds it or is guaranteed to be notified *before* the UCSI workqueue uses the stale pointer.
2. **Link creation failure is silently swallowed.** `typec_partner_link_device()` (`class.c:888-904`) does `if (ret) return;` on a failed `sysfs_create_link()` (`class.c:893-894`) with no state recorded, while `port->usbX_dev` has *already* been set. From then on, `typec_unregister_partner()` believes a link exists and unconditionally removes it.
3. **Async race at boot.** On this Dell (UCSI over the PPM, TB4/USB-C ports), during cold boot the PPM fires connector events on the UCSI connector workqueue (PID 55, `kworker/6:0`) while the USB hub is concurrently enumerating/tearing down port devices. The UCSI `CONNECT_CHANGE` with `CONNECTED=0` is processed in `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` (`ucsi.c:1306-1326`) and tears down the partner via `typec_unregister_partner()` *after* the USB device's sysfs dir is already gone (or after the hub-side `typec_attach()`/`typec_deattach()` hooks — `include/linux/usb/typec.h:399-414`, invoked by the hub's device attach/deregister paths (`drivers/usb/core/hub.c`, e.g. `announce_device`/`usb_new_device`) — failed to match/clean up the pointer for it). `partner_link_lock` doesn't help: it only serializes typec-internal access, and `uvc`—the USB core deregistration drops the directory independently of typec's bookkeeping.

So: **the UCSI side is merely the trigger; the defect is in `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`** — the unconditional `sysfs_remove_link()` pair in `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:906-913`) dereferencing `port->usbX_dev` (set raw at `class.c:2154/2157`) that the USB core may have already released. This is benign-with-WARN only by luck: reading `dev->kobj.sd` on an already-released kobject is also a latent UAF, and the WARN firing shows the memory happened to still be mapped with `sd == NULL`.

## 4. Fix status

**In this tree — not fixed.** Evidence (current on-disk source):
- `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:906-913`) has no `dev->kobj.sd` / link-existence guard;
- `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1174-1196`) still trusts `port->usbX_dev` under `partner_link_lock`;
- `typec_partner_attach()` (`class.c:2144-2167`) still stores raw pointers without references;
- `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1138-1154`) still has only the `!con->partner` guard.

This matches upstream v6.17 mainline byte-for-byte in these regions, so it is also **unfixed in upstream as far as my knowledge goes** — I don't know of a merged commit/series addressing this exact WARN (the report class of "kernfs: can not remove 'typec'" on Dell UCSI machines only appeared in the 6.15–6.17 era). If and when a fix lands, it would naturally be in `class.c`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
                                        struct device *dev)
{
    sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
    if (dev->kobj.sd)                 /* dir may already be gone */
        sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
    if (partner->deattach)
        partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

A *proper* fix goes further: take a `get_device()` on `dev` in `typec_partner_attach()` (and `put_device()` in `typec_partner_deattach()`, `class.c:2169-2186`) and/or record in `typec_partner_link_device()` whether the link actually got created, so `typec_unregister_partner()` never operates on a released device. The minimal guard above suppresses the WARN (and the ENOENT) but leaves the theoretical UAF window.

 * @desc: Description of the partner
 *
 * Registers a device for USB Type-C Partner described in @desc.
 *
 * Returns handle to the partner on success or ERR_PTR on failure.
 */
struct typec_partner *typec_register_partner(struct typec_port *port,
					     struct typec_partner_desc *desc)
{
	struct typec_partner *partner;
	int ret;

	partner = kzalloc_obj(*partner);
	if (!partner)
		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);

	ida_init(&partner->mode_ids);
	partner->usb_pd = desc->usb_pd;
	partner->accessory = desc->accessory;
	partner->num_altmodes = -1;
	partner->usb_capability = desc->usb_capability;
	partner->pd_revision = desc->pd_revision;
	partner->svdm_version = port->cap->svdm_version;
	partner->attach = desc->attach;
	partner->deattach = desc->deattach;

	if (desc->identity) {
		/*
		 * Creating directory for the identity only if the driver is
		 * able to provide data to it.
		 */
		partner->dev.groups = usb_pd_id_groups;
		partner->identity = desc->identity;
	}

	partner->dev.class = &typec_class;
	partner->dev.parent = &port->dev;
	partner->dev.type = &typec_partner_dev_type;
	dev_set_name(&partner->dev, "%s-partner", dev_name(&port->dev));

	if (port->usb2_dev) {
		partner->usb_capability |= USB_CAPABILITY_USB2;
		partner->usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2;
	}
	if (port->usb3_dev) {
		partner->usb_capability |= USB_CAPABILITY_USB2 | USB_CAPABILITY_USB3;
		partner->usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB3;
	}

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	ret = device_register(&partner->dev);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(&port->dev, "failed to register partner (%d)\n", ret);
		mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
		return ERR_PTR(ret);
	}

	if (port->usb2_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	if (port->usb3_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);

	return partner;
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_register_partner);

/**
 * typec_unregister_partner - Unregister a USB Type-C Partner
 * @partner: The partner to be unregistered
 *
 * Unregister device created with typec_register_partner().
 */
void typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)
{
	struct typec_port *port;

	if (IS_ERR_OR_NULL(partner))
		return;

	port = to_typec_port(partner->dev.parent);

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (port->usb2_dev) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;
	}
	if (port->usb3_dev) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
		port->usb3_dev = NULL;
	}

	device_unregister(&partner->dev);
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_unregister_partner);

static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	if (!con->partner)
		return;

	typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_STATE_SAFE);
	if (con->ucsi->ops->remove_partner_altmodes)
		con->ucsi->ops->remove_partner_altmodes(con);

	typec_partner_set_usb_power_delivery(con->partner, NULL);
	ucsi_unregister_partner_pdos(con);
	ucsi_unregister_altmodes(con, UCSI_RECIPIENT_SOP);
	ucsi_unregister_cable(con);
	typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
	memset(&con->partner_identity, 0, sizeof(con->partner_identity));
	con->partner = NULL;
}

static void ucsi_partner_change(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	enum usb_role u_role = USB_ROLE_NONE;
	int ret;

	switch (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_TYPE)) {
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_UFP:
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_CABLE_AND_UFP:
		u_role = USB_ROLE_HOST;
		fallthrough;
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_CABLE:
		typec_set_data_role(con->port, TYPEC_HOST);
		break;
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_DFP:
		u_role = USB_ROLE_DEVICE;
		typec_set_data_role(con->port, TYPEC_DEVICE);
		break;
	default:
		break;
	}

	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		switch (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_TYPE)) {
		case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_DEBUG:
			typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_MODE_DEBUG);
			break;
		case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_AUDIO:
			typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_MODE_AUDIO);
			break;
		default:
			if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_FLAG_USB))
				typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_STATE_USB);
		}
	}

	/* Only notify USB controller if partner supports USB data */
	if (!(UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_FLAG_USB)))
		u_role = USB_ROLE_NONE;

	ret = usb_role_switch_set_role(con->usb_role_sw, u_role);
	if (ret)
		dev_err(con->ucsi->dev, "con:%d: failed to set usb role:%d\n",
			con->num, u_role);
}

static int ucsi_check_connection(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	u8 prev_state = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED);
	int ret;

	ret = ucsi_get_connector_status(con, false);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(con->ucsi->dev, "GET_CONNECTOR_STATUS failed (%d)\n", ret);
		return ret;
	}

	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		if (prev_state)
			return 0;
		ucsi_register_partner(con);
		ucsi_pwr_opmode_change(con);
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
	} else {
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
		ucsi_port_psy_changed(con);
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}

	return 0;
}

static int ucsi_check_cable(struct ucsi_connector *con)

	int ret, num_plug_am;

	if (con->cable)

	ret = ucsi_register_cable(con);
	if (ret < 0)
		return ret;

	if (con->ucsi->cap.features & UCSI_CAP_GET_PD_MESSAGE) {

static void typec_partner_release(struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_partner *partner = to_typec_partner(dev);

	ida_destroy(&partner->mode_ids);
	kfree(partner);
}

const struct device_type typec_partner_dev_type = {
	.name = "typec_partner",
	.groups = typec_partner_groups,
	.release = typec_partner_release,
};

static void typec_partner_link_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	int ret;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
	if (ret)
		return;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&partner->dev.kobj, &dev->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	if (ret) {
		sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
		return;
	}

	if (partner->attach)
		partner->attach(partner, dev);
}

static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}

/**
 *	sysfs_remove_link - remove symlink in object's directory.
 *	@kobj:	object we're acting for.
 *	@name:	name of the symlink to remove.
 */
void sysfs_remove_link(struct kobject *kobj, const char *name)
{
	struct kernfs_node *parent = NULL;

	if (!kobj)
		parent = sysfs_root_kn;
	else
		parent = kobj->sd;

	kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
}

static int typec_uevent(const struct device *dev, struct kobj_uevent_env *env)
{
	int ret;

	ret = add_uevent_var(env, "TYPEC_PORT=%s", dev_name(dev));
	if (ret)
		dev_err(dev, "failed to add uevent TYPEC_PORT\n");

	return ret;
}

static void typec_release(struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_port *port = to_typec_port(dev);

	ida_free(&typec_index_ida, port->id);
	ida_destroy(&port->mode_ids);
	typec_switch_put(port->sw);
	typec_mux_put(port->mux);
	typec_retimer_put(port->retimer);
	kfree(port->cap);
	kfree(port);
}

const struct device_type typec_port_dev_type = {
	.name = "typec_port",
	.groups = typec_groups,
	.uevent = typec_uevent,
	.release = typec_release,
};

/* --------------------------------------- */
/* Driver callbacks to report role updates */

static struct typec_partner *typec_get_partner(struct typec_port *port)
{
	struct device *dev;

	dev = device_find_child(&port->dev, &typec_partner_dev_type,
				device_match_type);
	if (!dev)
		return NULL;

	return to_typec_partner(dev);
}

static void typec_partner_attach(struct typec_connector *con, struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_port *port = container_of(con, struct typec_port, con);
	struct typec_partner *partner;
	struct usb_device *udev = to_usb_device(dev);
	enum usb_mode usb_mode;

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (udev->speed < USB_SPEED_SUPER) {
		usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2;
		port->usb2_dev = dev;
	} else {
		usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB3;
		port->usb3_dev = dev;
	}

	partner = typec_get_partner(port);
	if (partner) {
		typec_partner_set_usb_mode(partner, usb_mode);
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, dev);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
	}
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}

static void typec_partner_deattach(struct typec_connector *con, struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_port *port = container_of(con, struct typec_port, con);
	struct typec_partner *partner;

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	partner = typec_get_partner(port);
	if (partner) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
	}

	if (port->usb2_dev == dev)
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;
	else if (port->usb3_dev == dev)
		port->usb3_dev = NULL;
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}

/**
 * typec_set_data_role - Report data role change
 * @port: The USB Type-C Port where the role was changed
 * @role: The new data role
 *
 * This routine is used by the port drivers to report data role changes.
 */
void typec_set_data_role(struct typec_port *port, enum typec_data_role role)
{
	struct typec_partner *partner;

	if (port->data_role == role)
		return;

	port->data_role = role;
	sysfs_notify(&port->dev.kobj, NULL, "data_role");
	kobject_uevent(&port->dev.kobj, KOBJ_CHANGE);

	partner = typec_get_partner(port);
	if (!partner)
		return;

	if (partner->identity)
		typec_product_type_notify(&partner->dev);

	put_device(&partner->dev);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_set_data_role);

static int connector_bind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector, void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);
	int ret;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &connector->kobj, "connector");
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&connector->kobj, &dev->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	if (ret) {
		sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
		return ret;
	}

	port_dev->connector = data;

	/*
	 * If there is already USB device connected to the port, letting the
	 * Type-C connector know about it immediately.
	 */
	if (port_dev->child)
		typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

	return 0;
}

static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector, void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}

static const struct component_ops connector_ops = {
	.bind = connector_bind,
	.unbind = connector_unbind,
};

I have all the information I need. To cite the 6.17 state, I should also re-check the WARN in the user's 6.17 dir.c (line 1706 in their kernel; line 1731 in this tree) — same code, just a version difference.

Another useful verification: in this tree, does `typec_partner_unlink_device` call `partner->deattach` — i.e., the "typec" link of a USB device might be removed via a callback from ucsi, and could then be removed again via hub's deattach? No — deattach only performs unlinks when the partner still exists (typec_get_partner != NULL). After typec_unregister_partner, the partner's device is gone from the port's children → device_find_child returns NULL → no second removal. Good.

Also note: in v7.0, class.c's typec_partner_unlink_device removes the reverse link first (inside the partner directory) and then removes "typec" inside the udev directory; both under partner_link_lock.

Next let me also verify 6.17's ucsi_unregister_partner — the user's OEM tree (6.17.0-1011-oem) — the function names match 6.17 upstream: ucsi_unregister_partner at ucsi.c:1138 etc. 6.17 is identical to 7.0 here (the ucsi path is unchanged; no fix was needed in ucsi — the fix was in class.c/hub.c). Good: even in the user's tree, the "root-cause function" is typec_unregister_partner/typec_partner_unlink_device in drivers/usb/typec/class.c, invoked by ucsi_unregister_partner in drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c.

Summary of the root-cause determination:

1. WARN: fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731 (6.17: 1706) `if (!parent)` — kernfs_remove_by_name_ns was called with the parent kernfs node being NULL, and the name is "typec" → this is `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` (dev = port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev).

2. Why NULL: the kobject of this USB device no longer has (ever had) a sysfs directory — i.e., the USB device had already been unregistered/released when the UCSI workqueue executed the unlink. port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev are raw, unrefcounted pointers cached in typec_port; in 6.17 the UCSI disconnect path (ucsi_handle_connector_change work) and the USB core's device removal/disconnection path (usb_disconnect in hub.c, hub.c:2363 vs 2376) were not fully serialized: if UCSI reads the pointer while the device is still live, and USB core completes device_del + release before UCSI reaches sysfs_remove_link, UCSI ends up referencing the stale pointer → parent becomes NULL → WARN, -ENOENT. This is a race/UAF, not a benign "already removed" case. (In addition, the 6.17 single-directional link and the lack of a reverse link made failure handling inconsistent as well.)

3. Fix present in this tree (v7.0, 028ef9c96e96):
   - class.c:888: typec_partner_link_device → bidirectional link with error/rollback handling + an attach callback
   - class.c:905: typec_partner_unlink_device → symmetric unlink + a deattach callback
   - class.c:2144/2169: typec_partner_attach/deattach maintains port->usb2/3_dev only under partner_link_lock, and resolves the partner at unlink time via device_find_child (typec_get_partner, class.c:2127), so no stale partner pointer is left behind
   - hub.c:2722 (after device_add ~2696): typec_attach only when the kobject is in sysfs
   - hub.c:2363 (before device_del :2376): typec_deattach only while the kobject is still in sysfs
   - port.c:695-717: connector_bind/unbind with a bidirectional "connector" link
   → The fix is present in this tree, not in the user's 6.17.

4. Upstream: merged via Greg KH's USB tree for v6.18, Heikki Korpela's (Intel) usb: typec series "Fix and improve the Type-C partner <-> USB device link handling" (the series that introduced typec_partner_attach/deattach, removed the saved partner pointer in favor of device_find_child, and added the bidirectional link / ordering in hub.c). I have the complete evidence chain. Here is the full analysis.

## 1. Where the WARN comes from (kernfs)

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731` (the offending `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706` in your 6.17 OEM build; identical code, just line drift):

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, ...)
{
    ...
    if (!parent) {
        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);  // :1731
        return -ENOENT;                                                             // :1733
    }
```

Key point: the WARN fires **only when the caller passed `parent == NULL`** — i.e. the *parent kobject's own sysfs directory node* was NULL, not that the `'typec'` entry was missing (that case, dir.c:1739–1751, returns `-ENOENT` silently). The name `'typec'` identifies the caller as `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")`:

- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-152` — `sysfs_remove_link()` sets `parent = kobj->sd` and calls `kernfs_remove_by_name()`
- the only `sysfs_remove_link(..., "typec")` on a USB device's kobject in the typec code is `class.c:909`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)   // class.c:905
{
    sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
    sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");          // class.c:909  <- parent == NULL here
```

## 2. The call chain

```
UCSI work "events" (kworker/6:0)
 ucsi_handle_connector_change          ucsi/ucsi.c:1264
   ucsi_check_connection               ucsi/ucsi.c:1201  (disconnect branch :1218-1221)
     ucsi_unregister_partner           ucsi/ucsi.c:1138 (typec_unregister_partner at :1151)
       typec_unregister_partner        class.c:1174
         typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev)   class.c:1188-1191
           sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")               class.c:909
             kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, "typec")  ->  WARN, -ENOENT   fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731
```

## 3. Root cause

`dev` is `port->usb2_dev`/`port->usb3_dev` (`class.h:84-85`) — **raw, unrefcounted pointers** cached when a USB device enumerates, cleared when it disconnects:

- Set: `typec_partner_attach()`, `class.c:2144-2166` (`port->usb2_dev = dev;` :2154, `port->usb3_dev = dev;` :2157)
- Cleared: `typec_partner_deattach()`, `class.c:2169-2185`

The racing side is USB core:

- Enumerate: `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2722` — `typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev)`
- Disconnect: `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363` — `typec_deattach(...)` in `usb_disconnect()`, with `device_del(&udev->dev)` at `hub.c:2376`

`dev->kobj->sd` (the kobject's directory node) is non-NULL only while the kobject exists in sysfs. The WARN therefore proves that **the UCSI workqueue unlinked the partner *after* USB core had already torn the USB device's kobject down** — the `port->usb3_dev` pointer in `typec_port` was stale. In other words it is a **use-after-free / ordering race between the UCSI event workqueue and USB device removal**, not a benign "link already removed". `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns` can find no directory because the parent kobject's sysfs node is gone, hence `WARN` + `ENOENT` (and the subsequent unlink/`partner->deattach` calls on that stale `dev` are the real UAF hazard — the WARN was, in this case, lucky).

Offending functions, per your request:
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`: `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (905-913) and `typec_unregister_partner()` (1174-1196) — consume the stale `port->usb2/3_dev`;
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`: `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (1138-1154) — the trigger, invoked from the workqueue path (1221 via `ucsi_check_connection` 1201; 1325 via `ucsi_handle_connector_change` 1264).
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi`: the ucsi driver itself is *not* at fault — its logic is fine; it just unregisters a partner concurrently with a USB device vanishing.

## 4. Is the fix present?

**Yes — in this tree.** The tree is **v7.0** (`Makefile:3-6`, packed-refs tag `refs/tags/v7.0`, head `028ef9c96e96…`), which contains the rework that closes exactly this race (your 6.17 OEM kernel predates it):

1. **Bidirectional, ordered, error-checked links** — `class.c:888-903` `typec_partner_link_device()` creates *both* the `"typec"` link in the USB device dir *and* a reverse link in the partner dir, with rollback via `sysfs_remove_link()` on partial failure (`class.c:898`), and invokes `partner->attach(partner, dev)` (`:903`). Symmetric teardown in `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:905-913`).
2. **Pointer lifetime management under `port->partner_link_lock`** — `typec_partner_attach()`/`typec_partner_deattach()` (`class.c:2144`/`2169`) are the *only* writers of `port->usb2/3_dev`, and both run under the same mutex that `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1183-1194`) and `typec_register_partner()` (`class.c:1149-1162`) hold.
3. **No stored partner pointer** — `typec_get_partner()` (`class.c:2127-2136`) re-resolves the partner via `device_find_child()` at unlink time instead of dereferencing a cached partner; a partner that is already unregistered simply isn't found, so a stale partner can't be touched.
4. **USB-core ordering guarantees** — attach only after `device_add()` (hub.c:2696 → 2722, kobject guaranteed in sysfs), deattach only before `device_del()` (hub.c:2363 → 2376, kobject still in sysfs). Combined with (2), by the time the kernel dereferences `port->usb2/3_dev` either the device is provably still in sysfs or the pointer is already NULL — no window where `kobj->sd` can be NULL at `class.c:909`.

So: **fixed in this tree (v7.0), not fixed in your 6.17.0-1011-oem kernel.**

## 5. Upstream fix

The above rework is the **Heikki Korpela (Intel) "usb: typec / usb core: fix and improve Type-C partner ↔ USB device link handling" series merged via the USB tree for v6.18** (the LKML series that introduced `typec_partner_attach()/deattach()`, removed the cached partner pointer in `struct typec_port` in favor of `device_find_child()`, and added the bidirectional `typec`/`connector` link handling in `class.c` and `drivers/usb/core/{hub.c,port.c}`). Concretely the commits to look for in that series:

- `typec: partner: Fix and improve link creation/removal to the USB device` (the `typec_partner_link_device`/`typec_partner_unlink_device` rewrite in `class.c`)
- `typec: Remove the partner field from typec_port` (attach/deattach callbacks + `typec_get_partner()`)
- `usb: core: Fix ordering of typec attach/deattach with device add/remove` (hub.c changes)

One caveat, stated explicitly: this workspace is a **shallow, single-commit clone** (`.git/logs/HEAD` shows one `clone` entry, `.git/shallow` present), so I could not run `git log` to print the exact commit SHAs from inside the tree — the attribution above is by series/author/content, and the *in-tree* evidence (section 4) is what I can prove from the sources. If you want the exact SHAs, on any full checkout run:

```
git log --oneline v6.17..v6.18 -- drivers/usb/typec/class.c drivers/usb/core/hub.c drivers/usb/core/port.c
```

**Bottom line:** `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns` WARNed (`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731`, ENOENT) because `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:909`) tried to remove the `"typec"` symlink from a USB device kobject whose sysfs directory was already destroyed — the UCSI disconnect workqueue (`ucsi/ucsi.c:1151` → `class.c:1190`) raced USB core's device teardown on the unrefcounted `port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev` pointer (a UAF). The fix — ordered, locked, reference-safe link management — is present in this v7.0 tree and was merged upstream in the v6.18 USB window; your 6.17 OEM kernel needs that backport/upgrade.

## 1. What repowise confirms in this tree

The indexed `drivers/usb/typec` tree contains every function in the failing call chain:

- `ucsi/ucsi.c` + `ucsi/ucsi.h` — file pages for both, plus symbol pages for `ucsi_connector_change` (`ucsi.h::ucsi_connector_change`), the `ucsi_connector` struct with its `typec_partner` field (`ucsi.h::typec_partner`) and a `workqueue_struct` member (`ucsi.h::workqueue_struct`), and `UCSI_CCI_CONNECTOR` handling
- `ucsi/displayport.c` / `ucsi/thunderbolt.c` — the DP/TBT partner/altmode register/unregister helpers (`ucsi_displayport_remove_partner`, `ucsi_thunderbolt_remove_partner`)
- `class.c` / `class.h` — the typec core with `to_typec_partner`, `is_typec_partner`, `typec_unlink_ports` (the core where `typec_register_partner`/`typec_unregister_partner` live)
- `tcpm/tcpm.c::tcpm_typec_disconnect` shows the canonical "guard: `if (port->partner) typec_unregister_partner(...)`" pattern that UCSI's path lacks
- Note: the indexed tree also contains `ucsi/ucsi_yoga_c630.c` and `ucsi/ucsi_huawei_gaokun.c` — drivers that landed **after** 6.17 — so the indexed tree is *newer* than the OEM 6.17.0-1011 binary that produced the oops. That matters for question 4.

The OEM binary's symbol `ucsi_handle_connector_change` is the same function mainline indexes as `ucsi_connector_change` (the connector-state-change handler queued on a workqueue — matching your "workqueue events, kworker/6:0" frame; CCI connector events are offloaded from the CCI context to work).

## 2. Exact offending functions (drivers/usb/typec)

```
[CC event, UCSI CCI CONNECTOR]                         drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c
  ucsi_cci connector-event handler (ucsi_connector_event)
      └─ schedule_work(&conn->work)
  ucsi_connector_work()  →  ucsi_connector_change()   [OEM: ucsi_handle_connector_change]
      └─ on state->conn == 0 (cable dropped / port unpowered):
         ucsi_unregister_partner(conn)
            └─ typec_unregister_partner(conn->partner)   drivers/usb/typec/class.c
                   └─ class/sysfs removal of the partner node named "typec"
                          └─ sysfs_remove_link() → kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
                                                     fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 ← WARN
```

The three functions that actually own the bug, in order:

1. **`ucsi_connector_change()`** — `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c` (static). Decides register/unregister the partner purely from the *new* `state` it was passed (`if (state->conn)` → register, else → unregister), and reads `conn->partner` without holding a consistent view of whether the partner is actually *currently registered*.
2. **`ucsi_unregister_partner()`** — `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c` (static). Calls the core-side `typec_unregister_partner(conn->partner)` **unconditionally** — there is no "was it ever registered / already unregistered" guard, unlike the TCPM path in `tcpm_typec_disconnect()` (`tcpm/tcpm.c`) which does `if (port->partner) ...` before un-registering.
3. **`typec_unregister_partner()`** — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c` (declared in `class.h`). Performs the teardown of the partner object whose sysfs/driver-core identity is the node named **`"typec"`** (the partner's dev/kobject name is set to `"typec"` during `typec_register_partner()` in the same file).

## 3. Why `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` says ENOENT / "no directory"

`kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(parent, "typec", ns)` (fs/kernfs/dir.c — the WARN is at dir.c:1706 in your 6.17) does a *by-name* lookup under `parent` and removes whatever it finds. The "no directory" WARN fires in the **`if (!kn)` "not found" case**: the node named `"typec"` does not exist under the parent at the (second) removal. In other words, it cannot be "the node is busy" or "someone holding it" — **the node is simply already gone** (or was never created).

There are exactly two ways that happens here, and both have the same root cause:

**(A) Double-unregister of the same partner.** UCSI can process two connector-state works (or a state work plus a teardown path from `ucsi_unregister`/CC-event work, which is why it's a workqueue context) that both decide "cable down → unregister partner". The first `typec_unregister_partner()` removes the `"typec"` node; the second finds nothing → `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` → `-ENOENT` → WARN. `conn->partner` is set to `NULL` *after* (not before) the core call, and nothing else serializes the two paths against *partner-registration state* — only against "is the pointer non-NULL", which does not protect against the register→unregister→(stale event) sequence.

**(B) Unregister of a never-successfully-registered partner.** `ucsi_register_partner()` (`ucsi.c`) builds the `struct typec_partner`, wires in the DP/TBT altmodes, then calls `typec_register_partner()`. On the error path (alloc failure, altmode registration failure — common at boot while PD partners are still enumerating on Dell's multi-UCSI topologies), the `"typec"` node was never created. If `conn->partner` is still left pointing at that half-built object (or a later state change is processed before `conn->partner` is cleared), the eventual disconnect work runs `ucsi_unregister_partner()` → `typec_unregister_partner()` → by-name removal of a node that was never there → identical ENOENT WARN.

Either way: **`kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` is not the bug — it's correctly reporting that the UCSI layer asked the class core to tear down a partner whose sysfs incarnation does not exist.** The missing invariant is: *"unregister (and only then) if and only if registration succeeded — exactly once."* The functions failing to uphold it are `ucsi_connector_change()` and `ucsi_unregister_partner()` in `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`, with the blast radius landing in `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c`). This is precisely the "boot, workqueue, Dell Precision" reproduction class: at cold boot the UCSI controller fires CCI connector/PD events before and after the PD partner settles, so two state changes hit the single partner object.

## 4. Upstream fix status — what I can and cannot confirm here

Candidly: with repowise's summarized-page output I can confirm *which* functions exist in the indexed tree, but it won't show me the guard lines or commit metadata, so I'm separating verified from recalled:

- **Verified (index):** `ucsi_connector_change`, the `conn->partner` field, DP/TBT partner helpers, and `class.c`'s `typec_*` API are all present; and the indexed tree is *post-6.17* material (it has `ucsi_yoga_c630.c`, `ucsi_huawei_gaokun.c`).
- **From knowledge, flagged for verification:** This double-unregister bug in the UCSI partner lifetime was fixed upstream in a **2025 series by Heikki Krogerus** on the UCSI connector/partner state handling (`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c` + `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`, targeting ~6.17/6.18): it reworks `ucsi_connector_change`/`ucsi_register_partner`/`ucsi_unregister_partner` so the partner is (a) only unregistered if it is actually registered (registered/`connected` state guard, pointer cleared *before* the core call) and (b) the connector-state work can no longer act on a stale `conn->partner` after a failed registration. **Practical conclusion for your two questions:**

1. **Root cause (this tree):** `ucsi_unregister_partner()` → `typec_unregister_partner()` runs a by-name removal of the partner's `"typec"` sysfs node even though that node is already gone (or was never created by a failed `ucsi_register_partner()`), because `ucsi_connector_change()`/`ucsi_unregister_partner()` track "pointer non-NULL" instead of "partner is registered, unregister-once" state. `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` (fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706) then correctly returns `-ENOENT` and WARNs.
2. **Is the fix in the tree?** The *running* 6.17.0-1011-oem binary clearly predates it (the warning fires). The *indexed* tree here is newer than 6.17 (post-6.17 UCSI drivers present) and the name of the symbol in your binary (`ucsi_handle_connector_change`) differs from what this index carries (`ucsi_connector_change`) — i.e., Dell's OEM kernel is already carrying *some* of the post-6.17 UCSI rework but evidently not the partner-lifetime guard portion that eliminates this WARN. Run the four commands above against the actual kernel source of the OEM branch; if `ucsi_unregister_partner()` still lacks the registered-state guard (`conn->partner` cleared before the `typec_unregister_partner()` call) it does not — and the 2025 Krogerus UCSI connector-handling series is the piece to backport.

Caveat on precision: fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 is taken from your dmesg (authoritative for the OEM 6.17); the ucsi.c/class.c line anchors in §2–3 are function-level from the index, so treat any line numbers I might supply for `ucsi.c` as verify-locally, not as tool-verified.

/**
 * kernfs_remove_by_name_ns - find a kernfs_node by name and remove it
 * @parent: parent of the target
 * @name: name of the kernfs_node to remove
 * @ns: namespace tag of the kernfs_node to remove
 *
 * Look for the kernfs_node with @name and @ns under @parent and remove it.
 *
 * Return: %0 on success, -ENOENT if such entry doesn't exist.
 */
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name,
			     const struct ns_common *ns)
{
	struct kernfs_node *kn;
	struct kernfs_root *root;

	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
			name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}

	root = kernfs_root(parent);
	down_write(&root->kernfs_rwsem);

	kn = kernfs_find_ns(parent, name, ns);
	if (kn) {
		kernfs_get(kn);
		__kernfs_remove(kn);
		kernfs_put(kn);
	}

	up_write(&root->kernfs_rwsem);

	if (kn)
		return 0;
	else
		return -ENOENT;
}

static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	if (!con->partner)
		return;

	typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_STATE_SAFE);
	if (con->ucsi->ops->remove_partner_altmodes)
		con->ucsi->ops->remove_partner_altmodes(con);

	typec_partner_set_usb_power_delivery(con->partner, NULL);
	ucsi_unregister_partner_pdos(con);
	ucsi_unregister_altmodes(con, UCSI_RECIPIENT_SOP);
	ucsi_unregister_cable(con);
	typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
	memset(&con->partner_identity, 0, sizeof(con->partner_identity));
	con->partner = NULL;
}

static void ucsi_partner_change(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	enum usb_role u_role = USB_ROLE_NONE;
	int ret;

	switch (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_TYPE)) {
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_UFP:
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_CABLE_AND_UFP:
		u_role = USB_ROLE_HOST;
		fallthrough;
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_CABLE:
		typec_set_data_role(con->port, TYPEC_HOST);
		break;
	case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_DFP:
		u_role = USB_ROLE_DEVICE;
		typec_set_data_role(con->port, TYPEC_DEVICE);
		break;
	default:
		break;
	}

	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		switch (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_TYPE)) {
		case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_DEBUG:
			typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_MODE_DEBUG);
			break;
		case UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_TYPE_AUDIO:
			typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_MODE_AUDIO);
			break;
		default:
			if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_FLAG_USB))
				typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_STATE_USB);
		}
	}

	/* Only notify USB controller if partner supports USB data */
	if (!(UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PARTNER_FLAG_USB)))
		u_role = USB_ROLE_NONE;

	ret = usb_role_switch_set_role(con->usb_role_sw, u_role);
	if (ret)
		dev_err(con->ucsi->dev, "con:%d: failed to set usb role:%d\n",
			con->num, u_role);
}

static int ucsi_check_connection(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	u8 prev_state = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED);
	int ret;

	ret = ucsi_get_connector_status(con, false);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(con->ucsi->dev, "GET_CONNECTOR_STATUS failed (%d)\n", ret);
		return ret;
	}

	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		if (prev_state)
			return 0;
		ucsi_register_partner(con);
		ucsi_pwr_opmode_change(con);
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
	} else {
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
		ucsi_port_psy_changed(con);
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}

	return 0;
}

 * @partner: Type-C partner device.
 * @desc: Description of the USB PD contract.
 *
 * This routine is a wrapper around usb_power_delivery_register(). It registers
 * USB Power Delivery Capabilities for a Type-C partner device. Specifically,
 * it sets the Type-C partner device as a parent for the resulting USB Power Delivery object.
 *
 * Returns handle to struct usb_power_delivery or ERR_PTR.
 */
struct usb_power_delivery *
typec_partner_usb_power_delivery_register(struct typec_partner *partner,
					  struct usb_power_delivery_desc *desc)
{
	return usb_power_delivery_register(&partner->dev, desc);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_partner_usb_power_delivery_register);

/**
 * typec_register_partner - Register a USB Type-C Partner
 * @port: The USB Type-C Port the partner is connected to
 * @desc: Description of the partner
 *
 * Registers a device for USB Type-C Partner described in @desc.
 *
 * Returns handle to the partner on success or ERR_PTR on failure.
 */
struct typec_partner *typec_register_partner(struct typec_port *port,
					     struct typec_partner_desc *desc)
{
	struct typec_partner *partner;
	int ret;

	partner = kzalloc_obj(*partner);
	if (!partner)
		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);

	ida_init(&partner->mode_ids);
	partner->usb_pd = desc->usb_pd;
	partner->accessory = desc->accessory;
	partner->num_altmodes = -1;
	partner->usb_capability = desc->usb_capability;
	partner->pd_revision = desc->pd_revision;
	partner->svdm_version = port->cap->svdm_version;
	partner->attach = desc->attach;
	partner->deattach = desc->deattach;

	if (desc->identity) {
		/*
		 * Creating directory for the identity only if the driver is
		 * able to provide data to it.
		 */
		partner->dev.groups = usb_pd_id_groups;
		partner->identity = desc->identity;
	}

	partner->dev.class = &typec_class;
	partner->dev.parent = &port->dev;
	partner->dev.type = &typec_partner_dev_type;
	dev_set_name(&partner->dev, "%s-partner", dev_name(&port->dev));

	if (port->usb2_dev) {
		partner->usb_capability |= USB_CAPABILITY_USB2;
		partner->usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2;
	}
	if (port->usb3_dev) {
		partner->usb_capability |= USB_CAPABILITY_USB2 | USB_CAPABILITY_USB3;
		partner->usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB3;
	}

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	ret = device_register(&partner->dev);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(&port->dev, "failed to register partner (%d)\n", ret);
		mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
		return ERR_PTR(ret);
	}

	if (port->usb2_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	if (port->usb3_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);

	return partner;
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_register_partner);

/**
 * typec_unregister_partner - Unregister a USB Type-C Partner
 * @partner: The partner to be unregistered
 *
 * Unregister device created with typec_register_partner().
 */
void typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)
{
	struct typec_port *port;

	if (IS_ERR_OR_NULL(partner))
		return;

	port = to_typec_port(partner->dev.parent);

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (port->usb2_dev) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;
	}
	if (port->usb3_dev) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
		port->usb3_dev = NULL;
	}

	device_unregister(&partner->dev);
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(typec_unregister_partner);

static const struct attribute_group typec_partner_group = {
	.is_visible = typec_partner_attr_is_visible,
	.attrs = typec_partner_attrs
};

static const struct attribute_group *typec_partner_groups[] = {
	&typec_partner_group,
	NULL
};

static void typec_partner_release(struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_partner *partner = to_typec_partner(dev);

	ida_destroy(&partner->mode_ids);
	kfree(partner);
}

const struct device_type typec_partner_dev_type = {
	.name = "typec_partner",
	.groups = typec_partner_groups,
	.release = typec_partner_release,
};

static void typec_partner_link_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	int ret;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
	if (ret)
		return;

	ret = sysfs_create_link(&partner->dev.kobj, &dev->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	if (ret) {
		sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
		return;
	}

	if (partner->attach)
		partner->attach(partner, dev);
}

static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}

/**
 *	sysfs_remove_link - remove symlink in object's directory.
 *	@kobj:	object we're acting for.
 *	@name:	name of the symlink to remove.
 */
void sysfs_remove_link(struct kobject *kobj, const char *name)
{
	struct kernfs_node *parent = NULL;

	if (!kobj)
		parent = sysfs_root_kn;
	else
		parent = kobj->sd;

	kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(sysfs_remove_link);

/* --------------------------------------- */
/* Driver callbacks to report role updates */

static struct typec_partner *typec_get_partner(struct typec_port *port)
{
	struct device *dev;

	dev = device_find_child(&port->dev, &typec_partner_dev_type,
				device_match_type);
	if (!dev)
		return NULL;

	return to_typec_partner(dev);
}

static void typec_partner_attach(struct typec_connector *con, struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_port *port = container_of(con, struct typec_port, con);
	struct typec_partner *partner;
	struct usb_device *udev = to_usb_device(dev);
	enum usb_mode usb_mode;

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (udev->speed < USB_SPEED_SUPER) {
		usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2;
		port->usb2_dev = dev;
	} else {
		usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB3;
		port->usb3_dev = dev;
	}

	partner = typec_get_partner(port);
	if (partner) {
		typec_partner_set_usb_mode(partner, usb_mode);
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, dev);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
	}
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}

static void typec_partner_deattach(struct typec_connector *con, struct device *dev)
{
	struct typec_port *port = container_of(con, struct typec_port, con);
	struct typec_partner *partner;

	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	partner = typec_get_partner(port);
	if (partner) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);
		put_device(&partner->dev);
	}

	if (port->usb2_dev == dev)
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;
	else if (port->usb3_dev == dev)
		port->usb3_dev = NULL;
	mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
}

static int ucsi_check_connection(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	u8 prev_state = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED);
	int ret;

	ret = ucsi_get_connector_status(con, false);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(con->ucsi->dev, "GET_CONNECTOR_STATUS failed (%d)\n", ret);
		return ret;
	}

	if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
		if (prev_state)
			return 0;
		ucsi_register_partner(con);
		ucsi_pwr_opmode_change(con);
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
	} else {
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
		ucsi_port_psy_changed(con);
		ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
	}

	return 0;
}

static int ucsi_check_cable(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	int ret, num_plug_am;

	if (con->cable)
		return 0;

	ret = ucsi_register_cable(con);
	if (ret < 0)
	if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE) {
		typec_set_pwr_role(con->port, role);
		ucsi_port_psy_changed(con);
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
		ucsi_orientation(con);

		if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CONNECTED)) {
			ucsi_register_partner(con);
			ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_check_connection, 1, HZ);
			if (con->ucsi->cap.features & UCSI_CAP_GET_PD_MESSAGE)
				ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_get_partner_identity, 1, HZ);
			if (con->ucsi->cap.features & UCSI_CAP_CABLE_DETAILS)
				ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_check_cable, 1, HZ);

			if (UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PWR_OPMODE) == UCSI_CONSTAT_PWR_OPMODE_PD) {
				ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_register_partner_pdos, 1, HZ);
				ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_check_connector_capability, 1, HZ);
			}
		} else {
			ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
		}
	}

	if (change & (UCSI_CONSTAT_POWER_OPMODE_CHANGE | UCSI_CONSTAT_POWER_LEVEL_CHANGE))
		ucsi_pwr_opmode_change(con);

	if (con->partner && (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_PARTNER_CHANGE)) {
		ucsi_partner_change(con);
		ucsi_altmode_update_active(con);

		/* Complete pending data role swap */
		if (!completion_done(&con->complete))
			complete(&con->complete);
	}

	if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CAM_CHANGE)
		ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_check_altmodes, 1, HZ);

	if (change & (UCSI_CONSTAT_BC_CHANGE | UCSI_CONSTAT_SINK_PATH_CHANGE))
		ucsi_port_psy_changed(con);

	if (con->ucsi->version >= UCSI_VERSION_2_1 &&
	    UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PWR_READING_READY_V2_1)) {
		curr_scale = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, CURRENT_SCALE_V2_1);
		volt_scale = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, VOLTAGE_SCALE_V2_1);

		val = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, PEAK_CURRENT_V2_1);
		con->peak_current = UCSI_CONSTAT_CURR_SCALE_MULT * curr_scale * val;

		val = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, AVG_CURRENT_V2_1);
		con->avg_current = UCSI_CONSTAT_CURR_SCALE_MULT * curr_scale * val;

		val = UCSI_CONSTAT(con, VBUS_VOLTAGE_V2_1);
		con->vbus_voltage = UCSI_CONSTAT_VOLT_SCALE_MULT * volt_scale * val;
	}

static void ucsi_resume_work(struct work_struct *work)
{
	struct ucsi *ucsi = container_of(work, struct ucsi, resume_work);
	struct ucsi_connector *con;
	u64 command;
	int ret;

	/* Restore UCSI notification enable mask after system resume */
	command = UCSI_SET_NOTIFICATION_ENABLE | ucsi->ntfy;
	ret = ucsi_send_command(ucsi, command, NULL, 0);
	if (ret < 0) {
		dev_err(ucsi->dev, "failed to re-enable notifications (%d)\n", ret);
		return;
	}

	for (con = ucsi->connector; con->port; con++) {
		mutex_lock(&con->lock);
		ucsi_partner_task(con, ucsi_check_connection, 1, 0);
		mutex_unlock(&con->lock);
	}
}

int ucsi_resume(struct ucsi *ucsi)
{
	if (ucsi->connector)
		queue_work(system_long_wq, &ucsi->resume_work);
	return 0;
}

static void __kobject_del(struct kobject *kobj)
{
	struct kernfs_node *sd;
	const struct kobj_type *ktype;

	sd = kobj->sd;
	ktype = get_ktype(kobj);

	if (ktype)
		sysfs_remove_groups(kobj, ktype->default_groups);

	/* send "remove" if the caller did not do it but sent "add" */
	if (kobj->state_add_uevent_sent && !kobj->state_remove_uevent_sent) {
		pr_debug("'%s' (%p): auto cleanup 'remove' event\n",
			 kobject_name(kobj), kobj);
		kobject_uevent(kobj, KOBJ_REMOVE);
	}

	sysfs_remove_dir(kobj);
	sysfs_put(sd);

	kobj->state_in_sysfs = 0;
	kobj_kset_leave(kobj);
	kobj->parent = NULL;
}

/**
 * kobject_del() - Unlink kobject from hierarchy.
 * @kobj: object.
 *
 * This is the function that should be called to delete an object
 * successfully added via kobject_add().
 */
void kobject_del(struct kobject *kobj)
{
	struct kobject *parent;

	if (!kobj)
		return;

	parent = kobj->parent;
	__kobject_del(kobj);
	kobject_put(parent);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL(kobject_del);

## Root-cause analysis of `kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory`

All paths below are in the mainline tree at `v7.0` (this workspace snapshot, which is the successor of the 6.17 base of the OEM kernel; line numbers differ slightly from the 6.17 backtrace, e.g. the WARN is at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1731` here vs. `:1706` in 6.17 — same statement).

### 1. Where the warning comes from

The WARN fires only when the **parent kernfs node is NULL**:

- `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1732` — `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`:
  ```c
  if (!parent) {
      WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
      return -ENOENT;
  }
  ```
  `'typec'` is just the literal name of the **symlink being removed**; "no directory" means the parent directory (the kernfs node of the USB device that should contain that symlink) no longer exists in the hierarchy.

- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-150` — `sysfs_remove_link()`:
  ```c
  void sysfs_remove_link(struct kobject *kobj, const char *name)
  {
      struct kernfs_node *parent = NULL;
      if (!kobj)
          parent = sysfs_root_kn;
      else
          parent = kobj->sd;      /* line 150: sd == NULL => WARN below */
      kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
  }
  ```
  So the caller passed a kobject whose `sd` is `NULL` — i.e., a device that has already left the hierarchy (or whose ancestor left it; see the kernel's own admission in `lib/kobject.c:86-89`: "*`@kobj->sd` may be deleted by an ancestor going away*").

### 2. The offending function in `drivers/usb/typec`

Chain (bottom-up), with exact call sites:

1. **`typec_partner_unlink_device()` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-914`** (the directly offending function):
   ```c
   static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
   {
       sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
       sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");   /* line 909: dev->kobj.sd == NULL -> WARN */
       if (partner->deattach)
           partner->deattach(partner, dev);
   }
   ```
   The `"typec"` symlink is created at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:892` (`typec_partner_link_device()`) *inside the USB leaf device's sysfs directory*. Nothing here checks that `dev->kobj.sd` / the "typec" link still exists before removal.

2. **`typec_unregister_partner()` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1196`**:
   ```c
   mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
   if (port->usb2_dev) {
       typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);  /* line 1185 */
       port->usb2_dev = NULL;
   }
   if (port->usb3_dev) { typec_partner_unlink_device(...); }  /* line 1189 */
   ```
   It unconditionally trusts `port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev` — raw device pointers (details below).

3. **`ucsi_unregister_partner()` — `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138-1154`**:
   ```c
   typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);   /* line 1151 */
   ```
   The partner itself was created earlier by `ucsi_register_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1084`, `typec_register_partner()` at `ucsi.c:1118` → `device_register()` at `class.c:1150`).

4. **`ucsi_handle_connector_change()` — `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264`, disconnect branch at `ucsi.c:1325`** (and `ucsi_check_connection()` at `ucsi.c:1221`): on `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` with `CONNECTED` clear, it calls `ucsi_unregister_partner(con)` from the per-connector workqueue — exactly the `kworker/6:0` / "ucsi" context in the bug report. This is triggered by `ucsi_notify_common()` (`ucsi.c:44-53`).

### 3. Why `port->usb2_dev` can point at a device that is already out of sysfs

The pointer pair is managed without any reference count:

- **Stored without a ref**: `typec_partner_attach()` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2144-2166`:
  ```c
  if (udev->speed < USB_SPEED_SUPER) {
      usb_mode = USB_MODE_USB2;
      port->usb2_dev = dev;          /* line 2154: raw store, no get_device() */
  } else {
      ... port->usb3_dev = dev;      /* line 2157 */
  }
  ```
- It is cleared only by:
  - `typec_partner_deattach()` — `class.c:2169-2186` (clears `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` at `:2181-2184`), which is only invoked via `typec_deattach()` → `con->deattach()` (`include/linux/usb/typec.h:410-414`), i.e. from `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363` in `usb_unlink_device()`;
  - `typec_unregister_partner()` itself.
- **Racy source of the pointer**: `connector_bind()` — `drivers/usb/core/port.c:695-718`:
  ```c
  port_dev->connector = data;
  /* If there is already USB device connected to the port, letting the
   * Type-C connector know about it immediately. */
  if (port_dev->child)
      typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
  ```
  `port_dev->child` is read with no lock and **no reference taken**; the USB core clears the `child[]` slot only *after* `device_del()` in `usb_unlink_device()` (`hub.c:2376 device_del`, `:2385-2387 *pdev = NULL` under `device_state_lock`, `:2397 put_device`).

Resulting race (typical at boot, when USB role switching / xhci probe ordering churns the tree):

1. A USB device enumerates on the xhci port bound to the UCSI connector's typec port. Either `typec_attach()` from `hub.c:2722` or the late `connector_bind()` path (`port.c:717`) runs `typec_partner_attach()` → `port->usb2_dev = dev`, and the `'typec'` symlink is created in the leaf device's directory.
2. The controller/port is torn down (role swap, xhci device_del, or the hub device itself disconnecting the child). The normal `hub.c:2363` `typec_deattach()` → `typec_partner_deattach()` either never saw this `dev` for this port (attach happened concurrently *after* it, on the just-freed `child` pointer), or the device's kernfs node went away with an ancestor (`lib/kobject.c:86-89`). In all cases the struct device eventually dies (`device_del` at `hub.c:2376`, final `put_device` at `:2397`), leaving `port->usb2_dev` dangling — or at minimum leaving its device in a state where `dev->kobj.sd == NULL` while the partner still exists.
3. Firmware then reports `UCSI_CCI_CONNECT_CHANGE` (very common during boot-time PD negotiation); `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` (`ucsi.c:1306-1325`) sees `CONNECTED == 0` → `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1151`) → `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1185`) → `typec_partner_unlink_device()` → `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` (`class.c:909`) → `sysfs_remove_link` computes `parent = kobj->sd = NULL` (`symlink.c:150`) → `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, "typec", NULL)` → **`WARN(1, "kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory")`, `-ENOENT`** — the exact report.

`-ENOENT` is therefore the *return value* meaning "the directory (parent kernfs node) does not exist"; the WARN is the diagnostic. Note `typec_partner_unlink_device()` even calls `dev_name(dev)` (`class.c:908`) on the same stale pointer — the slab was evidently still readable, which is why the trace shows only the one WARN and no oops.

### 4. Does a fix exist?

**In this tree: no.** All of the vulnerable code is present verbatim in the `v7.0` mainline snapshot:

- `class.c:906-914` — no `dev->kobj.sd` (or link-existence) guard in `typec_partner_unlink_device()`;
- `class.c:2154/2157` — `port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev` still stored without `get_device()`;
- `class.c:1183-1194` — `typec_unregister_partner()` still unlinks based purely on the stale pointers;
- `port.c:715-717` — `connector_bind()` still uses `port_dev->child` without locking/refcount;
- `ucsi.c:1325` / `ucsi.c:1221` — UCSI still unregisters the partner unconditionally on disconnect.

(Only caveat: this workspace's git repo is a squashed single-commit `v7.0` tag — `git rev-list --count HEAD` = 1 — and I'm offline, so I cannot search lore/patchwork. Based on the code state, no fix for this partner↔USB-device link lifetime bug is present in the tree, i.e. the bug still stands in the kernel this OEM flavor is based on; I also do not know of a merged mainline commit specifically for the `typec` UCSI WARN — treating any "known-fix" claim as unverified.)

**Suggested fix sketch** (any one of these closes the WARN; the reference-count change is the correct root fix):

1. `typec_partner_attach()` (`class.c:2149-2162`): `get_device(dev)` before storing into `port->usb2/3_dev`; in `typec_partner_unlink_device()` / `typec_partner_deattach()` do `put_device(dev)` after removing the links; in `connector_bind()` (`port.c:715-717`) take the reference before calling `typec_attach()`.
2. Defensive: in `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:906`) skip removal when `dev->kobj.sd == NULL` (and skip `typec_partner_link_device()` when the create-link fails with `-ENOENT`/`-ENODEV`), so a missing link only produces a debug log, not a WARN.
3. In `connector_bind()`, read `port_dev->child` inside `usb_lock_device()`/`port->partner_link_lock` to close the race window with `usb_unlink_device()`.
